CN-A1-1.speaker: marigold
CN-A1-1.text: Chapter one. Every field draws a map of where it has been. This one has a blank.

CN-A1-2.speaker: marigold
CN-A1-2.text: Horizontal collaboration: organisations at the same point in the supply chain, working together to gain what none could gain alone.

CN-A1-3.speaker: marigold
CN-A1-3.text: In the blank live the shippers, who own and send the goods: documented, but under-examined as a category.

CN-A1-4.speaker: marigold
CN-A1-4.text: Meanwhile parcels kept growing, the workforce barely grew, and where it has been measured, freight does more than its share of the harm.

CN-A1-5.speaker: marigold
CN-A1-5.text: The old remedy, competitors' parcels on one van, has mostly died. The survivors were driven by a single commercial enterprise.

CN-A1-6.speaker: marigold
CN-A1-6.text: And this is your old idea: the Big Fierce Animal, the large carrier that stands alone because it takes everything within reach.

CN-A1-7.speaker: marigold
CN-A1-7.text: Freight FM is on air, and Vera Static wants one answer before the news: where are the shippers?

CN-A1-8.speaker: marigold
CN-A1-8.text: Across the street, someone is taking notes. You'll meet her properly at the end.

CN-A1-9.speaker: marigold
CN-A1-9.text: Your job in the Blank Quarter: find the shippers, clock the traffic, and say the one sentence out loud.

CN-A1-T1.speaker: marigold
CN-A1-T1.text: Off air, the red lamp goes dark. Vera asks the question she kept off the radio.

CN-A1-T2.speaker: marigold
CN-A1-T2.text: The thesis was not designed to reach the conclusions it reaches. Expect to be asked about that.

CN-K1.speaker: marigold
CN-K1.text: The Blank Quarter is coloured in. Here is its line, word for word.

CN-K1-NEXT.speaker: marigold
CN-K1-NEXT.text: Next time: Archive Hill, where one search string meets the shelf it missed.

CA-K1-VERA.speaker: vera
CA-K1-VERA.text: Back on air before the Hall. Keep that parcel dry, yeah?

CA-K1-ANIMAL.speaker: animal
CA-K1-ANIMAL.text: Seven districts? I'm still bigger than all of them.

VR-g-The_gap.speaker: marigold
VR-g-The_gap.text: The gap. The shipper side of horizontal collaboration documented but under-examined as a category, and not set beside the carrier side.

SC-1.1-L01.speaker: vera
SC-1.1-L01.text: Freight FM, live and loud. Courier: horizontal collaboration, in plain English?

SC-1.1-L03.speaker: vera
SC-1.1-L03.text: And who did the field actually study?

SC-1.1-L05.speaker: vera
SC-1.1-L05.text: The newest reviews must file them somewhere, surely.

SC-1.1-L07.speaker: vera
SC-1.1-L07.text: Any case of carriers starting one together and measuring the result?

SC-1.1-FR.speaker: vera
SC-1.1-FR.text: Off mic for a sec: what was that question again?

SC-1.2-L02.speaker: vera
SC-1.2-L02.text: Got a caller on the line. Says: just put everyone's parcels on one van.

SC-1.2-FR.speaker: vera
SC-1.2-FR.text: That caller's back on the line: how many ever ran?

SC-1.3-L01.speaker: vera
SC-1.3-L01.text: Your whole thesis, one sentence. No pressure. Go.

SC-1.3-L05.speaker: vera
SC-1.3-L05.text: And the plan to get there?

SC-1.3-L07.speaker: vera
SC-1.3-L07.text: Split into links, each with a scorecard?

SC-1.3-FR.speaker: vera
SC-1.3-FR.text: Quick one off the card: which objective is 1B?

CARD-g-The_chain.speaker: marigold
CARD-g-The_chain.text: The chain. The five linked concepts: overlap, the boundary of sharing, the binder, power and the holder.

TP-A1-L01.speaker: vera
TP-A1-L01.text: Off air now. Straight up: did you plan these conclusions?

BA-A1-before-g-The_four_pillars.speaker: marigold
BA-A1-before-g-The_four_pillars.text: The four pillars. Trust, efficiency, innovation and sustainability: the framework the 2024 fieldwork was designed under, which the data replaced.

BA-A1-before-g-The_big_fierce_animal.speaker: marigold
BA-A1-before-g-The_big_fierce_animal.text: The big fierce animal. The author's 2022 image, used in his own way and not Colinvaux's: the large carrier stands alone because it takes everything within reach, while small operators share. The data corrected it to overlap; 6.4 keeps it as an image of territory.

BA-A1-after-ch1-tp.speaker: marigold
BA-A1-after-ch1-tp.text: What keeps a large carrier alone is not its size but overlap: at home it competes with everyone for the same customers (4.2, 6.4). The four pillars and that first idea both gave way to the chain set out in 1.5.

MI-A1-I1.speaker: vera
MI-A1-I1.text: Hear that growl? The Big Fierce Animal wants to know which idea the data corrected.

MI-A1-I2.speaker: vera
MI-A1-I2.text: Listener at a locker wants to know how common that is.

MI-A1-I3.speaker: vera
MI-A1-I3.text: Newsdesk wants your count of arrangements. On the hour, please.

MI-A1-I4.speaker: vera
MI-A1-I4.text: My producer's asking how many times the transcripts were coded.

SM-A1-I1.speaker: vera
SM-A1-I1.text: Late show caller, proper night owl: how many of those reviewed studies were models?

RH-A1-LEAD.speaker: marigold
RH-A1-LEAD.text: Dr Tally, passing, stops at your handlebars.

RH-A1-FB1.speaker: dr_tally
RH-A1-FB1.text: That's it: documented, under-examined, never side by side, and not resting on your own review.

RH-A1-FB2.speaker: dr_tally
RH-A1-FB2.text: Overclaims. Shippers are documented; the gap is that they are under-examined as a category.

RH-A1-FB3.speaker: dr_tally
RH-A1-FB3.text: Rests on your own review. The newest reviews show the gap independently.

EC-A1-INTRO.speaker: marigold
EC-A1-INTRO.text: The examiners have set up a table outside Freight FM. Answer aloud, then reveal.

OA-A1.speaker: vera
OA-A1.text: Your aim and your question, in your own words. Mic's yours.

TPQ-ch1.speaker: marigold
TPQ-ch1.text: What keeps a large carrier alone is not its size but overlap: at home it competes with everyone for the same customers (4.2, 6.4). The four pillars and that first idea both gave way to the chain set out in 1.5.

FM-ASK-A1.speaker: marigold
FM-ASK-A1.text: Which side of the map did everyone leave blank?

RADIO-A1-IN.speaker: vera
RADIO-A1-IN.text: Vera Static, Freight FM. The Blank Quarter's foggy tonight, so ride slow and look out for shippers.

RADIO-A1-OUT.speaker: vera
RADIO-A1-OUT.text: That's the fog lifting. Proper work, courier. Next stop, Archive Hill.

EQ-ch1-eq1.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch1-eq1.text: Your definition of horizontal collaboration includes shippers and public bodies. Why so wide?

EQ-ch1-eq2.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch1-eq2.text: What is the gap, in one sentence?

EQ-ch1-eq3.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch1-eq3.text: Why Europe, when one of your interviews is in India?

EQ-ch1-eq4.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch1-eq4.text: You worked on GREEN-LOG. Isn't that a conflict of interest?

EQ-ch1-eq5.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch1-eq5.text: What's your unit of analysis, and why not the firm?

QZ-ch1-q1.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch1-q1.text: What question does 1.1 put to the field's map?

QZ-ch1-q2.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch1-q2.text: Of the 89 studies Aloui and colleagues (2021) reviewed, how many were models?

QZ-ch1-q3.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch1-q3.text: In Britain in 2024-25, what share of parcels went to a locker or a shop rather than a door?

QZ-ch1-q4.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch1-q4.text: In the 2005 scoping study, how many of the 67 consolidation schemes with a usable record had ever operated?

QZ-ch1-q6.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch1-q6.text: How many accounts of arrangements did the thesis code (Appendix H)?

QZ-ch1-q7.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch1-q7.text: What was the author's 2022 idea that the data corrected?

QZ-ch1-q8.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch1-q8.text: How many times were the transcripts coded?

KF-ch1-01.speaker: marigold
KF-ch1-01.text: The two most recent systematic reviews of the field sort it by infrastructure, technology, sustainability and cold chain, and neither has a category for who begins a collaboration.

KF-ch1-02.speaker: marigold
KF-ch1-02.text: The review that sorted the field's evidence by method found that almost all its studies were models.

KF-ch1-03.speaker: marigold
KF-ch1-03.text: Across the 2023 review and its 2026 update, no single case shows carriers beginning a collaboration among themselves and reporting a measured result from it.

KF-ch1-04.speaker: marigold
KF-ch1-04.text: German carriers' parcel, express and courier shipments grew between 2019 and 2024, by the trade body's own count.

KF-ch1-05.speaker: marigold
KF-ch1-05.text: The European Union's postal and courier workforce barely grew in a decade.

KF-ch1-06.speaker: marigold
KF-ch1-06.text: Freight's harm runs ahead of its share of traffic: in Bordeaux, freight's share of vehicle-kilometres produced a larger share of the carbon dioxide.

KF-ch1-07.speaker: marigold
KF-ch1-07.text: In Britain in 2024-25, a share of parcels went to a locker or a shop rather than a door: one parcel in eight already ends at a point, the kind of shared point the thesis returns to.

KF-ch1-08.speaker: marigold
KF-ch1-08.text: Europe's cities had low-emission and zero-emission zones by October 2021, but few had a logistics plan or collected logistics data.

KF-ch1-09.speaker: marigold
KF-ch1-09.text: A scoping study for the British government counted consolidation schemes with a usable record by 2005; few had ever operated and fewer had been evaluated in any quantified way.

KF-ch1-10.speaker: marigold
KF-ch1-10.text: Padua's Cityporto, a surviving consolidation centre, opened in 2004, has needed no public money since 2007 and grew its deliveries.

KF-ch1-11.speaker: marigold
KF-ch1-11.text: The interviews span eleven countries, ten of them European; the eleventh, India, is a comparator. The interviews were held between July and September 2024 and the survey ran from February 2024 to April 2025.

KF-ch1-12.speaker: marigold
KF-ch1-12.text: Each link is tested in a chapter and carries a count of the twenty-six interviews (for, against, mixed, silent).

KF-ch1-13.speaker: marigold
KF-ch1-13.text: Of the 117 accounts of arrangements, most were held together by something outside the parties; few by the parties' own trust, one of which has dissolved.

KF-ch1-14.speaker: marigold
KF-ch1-14.text: Across the open locker networks, those held by a firm that sells no delivery reach on average about twice the share of a country's main carriers that rival-held ones do.

CN-A2-1.speaker: marigold
CN-A2-1.text: Chapter two. Archive Hill, where the field keeps its papers, and where a search finds only what it can see.

CN-A2-2.speaker: marigold
CN-A2-2.text: In the first review, one search string was cast across several databases and screened, stage by stage, down to a small set of studies.

CN-A2-3.speaker: marigold
CN-A2-3.text: Run again, it returns none of the papers in the field's own citation trail. A string finds only what it can see.

CN-A2-4.speaker: marigold
CN-A2-4.text: Corrected, it ran again in an open index anyone can use. Most of what it found names no one who begins.

CN-A2-5.speaker: marigold
CN-A2-5.text: Ada Stacks keeps the trail. She knows which shelves are empty, and exactly why.

CN-A2-6.speaker: marigold
CN-A2-6.text: The field's models put the biggest prize where rivals share the most customers. Remember that. The carriers have something to say about it.

CN-A2-7.speaker: marigold
CN-A2-7.text: Between the shelves, someone is reading the same review, pen ready. He hunts overclaims first.

CN-A2-8.speaker: marigold
CN-A2-8.text: Your job on Archive Hill: what the string caught, the shelf it missed, and the condition rivals pool under.

CN-A2-T1.speaker: marigold
CN-A2-T1.text: Ada has read the field's models and the field's carriers side by side. Now she holds a page to the light.

CN-A2-T2.speaker: marigold
CN-A2-T2.text: Hold on to it. In Red Cell Square, this paradox meets its mirror.

CN-K2.speaker: marigold
CN-K2.text: Archive Hill is coloured in. Here is its line, word for word.

CN-K2-NEXT.speaker: marigold
CN-K2-NEXT.text: Next time: Method Works, where the question is built before the answer.

CA-K2-ADA.speaker: ada
CA-K2-ADA.text: Every shelf you need is in the Archive Library. Come back any time.

CA-K2-ANIMAL.speaker: animal
CA-K2-ANIMAL.text: Models. I'd still never share my doors.

VR-ch2-tp.speaker: marigold
VR-ch2-tp.text: That is the tension the rest of this chapter follows: the field's mathematics needs overlap, and the field's carriers will not have it.

SC-2.1-L01.speaker: ada
SC-2.1-L01.text: Your first review: one string, six databases, five rounds of screening.

SC-2.1-L02.speaker: ada
SC-2.1-L02.text: Mind the databases: more were searched than contributed.

SC-2.1-L04.speaker: ada
SC-2.1-L04.text: Mostly models and reviews, and in most of them nobody begins the collaboration at all.

SC-2.1-FR.speaker: ada
SC-2.1-FR.text: Here's the first count. Slide it back with your answer.

CARD-g-Card.speaker: marigold
CARD-g-Card.text: Card. The author's reading note on each paper of the review.

SC-2.2-L01.speaker: ada
SC-2.2-L01.text: The test: the field's own citation trail on horizontal collaboration. Your old string returns none of it.

SC-2.2-L03.speaker: ada
SC-2.2-L03.text: ...its string couldn't find them, bar a few exceptions.

SC-2.2-L04.speaker: ada
SC-2.2-L04.text: And even in the corrected search, shippers or receivers begin the fewest.

SC-2.2-FR.speaker: ada
SC-2.2-FR.text: I've run the old string again. Call the result.

SC-2.3-L01.speaker: ada
SC-2.3-L01.text: Here's the tension. In the models, network profit rises with overlap.

SC-2.3-L03.speaker: ada
SC-2.3-L03.text: Your field's definition always let shippers in. Its models made them a demand point, not an actor.

SC-2.3-L04.speaker: ada
SC-2.3-L04.text: The field at its strongest: most who answered didn't want an independent third party.

SC-2.3-L06.speaker: ada
SC-2.3-L06.text: Saving plus penalty must cover exposure plus the wall, or rivals don't pool.

SC-2.3-FR.speaker: ada
SC-2.3-FR.text: One letter on the chalkboard is smudged. Fill it in.

TP-A2-L01.speaker: ada
TP-A2-L01.text: Hold the page to the light. Overlap runs through the evidence like a watermark.

TP-A2-L02.speaker: ada
TP-A2-L02.text: And here it is, in your words.

BA-A2-before-ch2-09.speaker: marigold
BA-A2-before-ch2-09.text: The models put the prize exactly where the interviews put the refusal: Berger and Bierwirth's network profit for three carriers rises with the overlap of their areas.

BA-A2-after-ch2-tp.speaker: marigold
BA-A2-after-ch2-tp.text: That is the tension the rest of this chapter follows: the field's mathematics needs overlap, and the field's carriers will not have it.

MI-A2-I1.speaker: ada
MI-A2-I1.text: The new catalogue needs its final count.

MI-A2-I2.speaker: ada
MI-A2-I2.text: A shipper knocks at the archive door. How many papers let them begin?

MI-A2-I3.speaker: ada
MI-A2-I3.text: See this boundary on the map? Whose theory draws it?

MI-A2-I4.speaker: ada
MI-A2-I4.text: A locker inspector asks how the rules define 'neutral'.

SM-A2-I1.speaker: ada
SM-A2-I1.text: A little one asked me why the kiosk looks like a blood cell. Help me out.

RH-A2-LEAD.speaker: marigold
RH-A2-LEAD.text: Professor Kerbstone looks up from a reading desk.

RH-A2-FB1.speaker: prof_kerbstone
RH-A2-FB1.text: Own the blind spot, then show what you built on it.

RH-A2-FB2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
RH-A2-FB2.text: Over-concedes. You kept the old studies and their criteria; the blind spot became the starting point.

RH-A2-FB3.speaker: prof_kerbstone
RH-A2-FB3.text: Denies the gap. The old string could not find those papers at all. Say so first.

EC-A2-INTRO.speaker: marigold
EC-A2-INTRO.text: Two reading desks pushed together: the examiners are waiting. Answer aloud, then reveal.

OA-A2.speaker: vera
OA-A2.text: The overlap paradox, in two sentences. Go on.

TPQ-ch2.speaker: marigold
TPQ-ch2.text: That is the tension the rest of this chapter follows: the field's mathematics needs overlap, and the field's carriers will not have it.

FM-ASK-A2.speaker: marigold
FM-ASK-A2.text: Why won't the vans that could save the most share?

RADIO-A2-IN.speaker: vera
RADIO-A2-IN.text: Archive Hill traffic: heavy on paper, light on shippers. Mind the shelves.

RADIO-A2-OUT.speaker: vera
RADIO-A2-OUT.text: Archive Hill, done and dusted. Ada says the quiet's yours any time.

EQ-ch2-eq1.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch2-eq1.text: Your own 2023 review missed the collaboration literature. Doesn't that undermine it?

EQ-ch2-eq2.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch2-eq2.text: Can the forty-nine and the 241 really be compared?

EQ-ch2-eq3.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch2-eq3.text: State the trust position you depart from at its strongest.

EQ-ch2-eq4.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch2-eq4.text: Eight bodies of theory. Isn't that a patchwork?

EQ-ch2-eq5.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch2-eq5.text: Your count of power in the update assumes your own claim, doesn't it?

QZ-ch2-q1.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch2-q1.text: How many records did the 2023 review start from?

QZ-ch2-q2.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch2-q2.text: Run again in OpenAlex, how many of the twelve papers in the field's citation trail does the 2022 string return?

QZ-ch2-q3.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch2-q3.text: How many papers did the 2026 update retain?

QZ-ch2-q4.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch2-q4.text: In how many of the 241 papers does a shipper or receiver begin the collaboration?

QZ-ch2-q5.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch2-q5.text: Which theory explains the boundary of sharing?

QZ-ch2-q6.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch2-q6.text: In the condition S + P ≥ L + W, what is W?

QZ-ch2-q7.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch2-q7.text: In Holguín-Veras's data, who set delivery times in forty per cent of cases?

QZ-ch2-q8.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch2-q8.text: How does the thesis use the image of the red blood cell?

QZ-ch2-q9.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch2-q9.text: How do the parcel-point rules the thesis reviewed define a neutral point?

KF-ch2-01.speaker: marigold
KF-ch2-01.text: The 2023 review put one search string to six databases in September 2022; five stages of screening reduced the records to forty-nine studies.

KF-ch2-02.speaker: marigold
KF-ch2-02.text: The forty-nine studies by type: reviews, conceptual frameworks, models and simulations, empirical studies and reports.

KF-ch2-03.speaker: marigold
KF-ch2-03.text: In at least thirty-two of the forty-nine no one begins the collaboration; counted by initiator, twenty-three cards name no one and only one, the 1996 paper, codes a shipper.

KF-ch2-04.speaker: marigold
KF-ch2-04.text: The only measured rounds in the forty-nine: Allen and colleagues tracked London parcel vans that had never collaborated.

KF-ch2-05.speaker: marigold
KF-ch2-05.text: Twelve papers sit inside the field's own citation trail on horizontal collaboration; run again in OpenAlex, the 2022 string returns none of them.

KF-ch2-06.speaker: marigold
KF-ch2-06.text: The 2026 update ran six strings in OpenAlex's title-and-abstract field and retained 241 papers; nine were among the forty-nine.

KF-ch2-07.speaker: marigold
KF-ch2-07.text: Of the other 231 papers, the 2022 string returns only thirty-nine; so, with at most eight exceptions, the 2023 review did not weigh these papers and reject them: its string could not find them.

KF-ch2-08.speaker: marigold
KF-ch2-08.text: Who begins the collaboration in the 241: most name no initiator; among those that do, shippers or receivers are the fewest.

KF-ch2-09.speaker: marigold
KF-ch2-09.text: The models put the prize exactly where the interviews put the refusal: Berger and Bierwirth's network profit for three carriers rises with the overlap of their areas.

KF-ch2-10.speaker: marigold
KF-ch2-10.text: Of three consolidation centres van Duin and colleagues compared, the city-begun one lived on a subsidy; the landlord's made a profit; the retailers' broke even once a two-year grant ended. The carriers took part in none.

KF-ch2-11.speaker: marigold
KF-ch2-11.text: The field's position at its strongest: Cruijssen, Cools and Dullaert's survey of Flemish providers, in which most respondents did not want an independent third party to coordinate.

KF-ch2-12.speaker: marigold
KF-ch2-12.text: Holguín-Veras showed the receiver decides: who set delivery times, and how few carriers could pass a toll on.

KF-ch2-13.speaker: marigold
KF-ch2-13.text: The rules that certify a shared parcel point as neutral define it by who may use it, not by who holds it; and holders change: an Austrian network held by firms that sell no delivery was bought by Deutsche Post.

KF-ch2-14.speaker: marigold
KF-ch2-14.text: The thesis extends the coalition models' stability condition: rivals pool only when the saving plus the penalty for staying out covers the exposure of customers, brand or data plus the cost of the wall that stops it.

CN-A3-1.speaker: marigold
CN-A3-1.text: Chapter three. Method Works, where the question is built before the answer.

CN-A3-2.speaker: marigold
CN-A3-2.text: First the paradigm, critical realism. Then a retroductive approach: from the regularity to the mechanism that would produce it.

CN-A3-3.speaker: marigold
CN-A3-3.text: A design in four stages, each stage's evidence feeding the next, in the order the method guide recommends.

CN-A3-4.speaker: marigold
CN-A3-4.text: The people were chosen for the question, not the industry: those who convene, fund, regulate, study and broker collaborations.

CN-A3-5.speaker: marigold
CN-A3-5.text: Clement Stamp keeps the consent slips and the ethics approval. He stamps everything twice.

CN-A3-6.speaker: marigold
CN-A3-6.text: Sam and Sal Whistle mark the same match apart, then settle every disputed call.

CN-A3-7.speaker: marigold
CN-A3-7.text: And Polly's survey runs on the side, read for scale and nothing more. It tests no link.

CN-A3-8.speaker: marigold
CN-A3-8.text: Up on the gantry, the note-taker from the Blank Quarter is back. She knows every table by heart.

CN-A3-9.speaker: marigold
CN-A3-9.text: Your job at Method Works: the blueprint, the permits, the microphones, the codings. And the Methods Academy over the road.

CN-A3-T1.speaker: marigold
CN-A3-T1.text: Your working claim walks onto the pitch. The second coding is the referee, and it has red cards ready.

CN-A3-T2.speaker: marigold
CN-A3-T2.text: Brand and size go off. Overlap and the boundary of sharing come on, and the codebook is rewritten from what survived.

CN-K3.speaker: marigold
CN-K3.text: Method Works is coloured in. Here is its line, word for word.

CN-K3-NEXT.speaker: marigold
CN-K3-NEXT.text: Next time: Witness Court, where your old idea stands trial.

VR-ch3-tp.speaker: marigold
VR-ch3-tp.text: That second coding did not sustain two of the claim's clauses, brand and size, and produced two regularities the claim had not named, overlap and the boundary of sharing; the codebook of Table 3.5 was rewritten from its results.

SC-3.1-L01.speaker: sam
SC-3.1-L01.text: Critical realism first: markets and customers exist whether or not anyone describes them well.

SC-3.1-L02.speaker: sal
SC-3.1-L02.text: Then retroduction: from the pattern to the mechanism that would produce it, tested against the cases that ought to break it.

SC-3.1-FR.speaker: sam
SC-3.1-FR.text: Sal's holding up the rulebook: which mode of inference?

SC-3.2-L01.speaker: clement
SC-3.2-L01.text: Approved: your guide, with a working script beside it.

SC-3.2-L03.speaker: sam
SC-3.2-L03.text: Online, in English, every one conducted by you.

SC-3.2-L04.speaker: polly
SC-3.2-L04.text: And my survey? Read for scale only. It tests no link.

SC-3.2-FR.speaker: clement
SC-3.2-FR.text: Polly's waving her clipboard at me: how many responses count?

SC-3.3-L01.speaker: sam
SC-3.3-L01.text: First coding: the guide's headings. Second: your working claim.

SC-3.3-L02.speaker: sal
SC-3.3-L02.text: Third: the five-concept codebook. Every transcript read a second time, blind to the first.

SC-3.3-L04.speaker: sam
SC-3.3-L04.text: Declined every time. Counted as declined, not as absent.

SC-3.3-FR.speaker: sam
SC-3.3-FR.text: My scoreboard's flickering. How many stances agreed?

CARD-g-The_four_pillars.speaker: marigold
CARD-g-The_four_pillars.text: The four pillars. Trust, efficiency, innovation and sustainability: the framework the 2024 fieldwork was designed under, which the data replaced.

CARD-g-The_working_claim_of_2026.speaker: marigold
CARD-g-The_working_claim_of_2026.text: The working claim of 2026. That the last mile is a brand asset, that size sorts willingness, that working arrangements run on substitutes for trust, that the power sits with shippers and cities and that time can do what pooling was asked to. The second coding tested it; brand and size fell.

TP-A3-L04.speaker: sam
TP-A3-L04.text: Overlap and the boundary of sharing. The codebook is rewritten from what survived.

BA-A3-before-g-The_working_claim_of_2026.speaker: marigold
BA-A3-before-g-The_working_claim_of_2026.text: The working claim of 2026. That the last mile is a brand asset, that size sorts willingness, that working arrangements run on substitutes for trust, that the power sits with shippers and cities and that time can do what pooling was asked to. The second coding tested it; brand and size fell.

BA-A3-after-ch3-05.speaker: marigold
BA-A3-after-ch3-05.text: The second coding did not sustain two clauses of the working claim, brand and size, and produced two regularities the claim had not named, overlap and the boundary of sharing.

MI-A3-I1.speaker: sal
MI-A3-I1.text: Name the clauses that got red cards.

MI-A3-I2.speaker: sal
MI-A3-I2.text: We've replayed the changes. Which one changed the answer?

SM-A3-I1.speaker: sam
SM-A3-I1.text: I timed the interviews. The median?

RH-A3-LEAD.speaker: marigold
RH-A3-LEAD.text: Dr Tally is waiting by the blueprints, pen uncapped.

RH-A3-FB1.speaker: dr_tally
RH-A3-FB1.text: Both alternatives dismissed for a reason. That's the answer.

RH-A3-FB2.speaker: dr_tally
RH-A3-FB2.text: Overclaims. A mechanism named from these accounts generalises to the mechanism, not to a population.

RH-A3-FB3.speaker: dr_tally
RH-A3-FB3.text: Wrong mode. The inference is retroduction: pattern to mechanism, tested against cases that ought to break it.

RH2-A3-LEAD.speaker: marigold
RH2-A3-LEAD.text: Dr Tally leans over the coding desk.

RH2-A3-FB2.speaker: dr_tally
RH2-A3-FB2.text: Denies it. Nobody escapes it. Name it, then show the safeguards.

RH2-A3-FB3.speaker: dr_tally
RH2-A3-FB3.text: Over-concedes. The later codings, the blind second readings and the evidence against are your safeguards.

EC-A3-INTRO.speaker: marigold
EC-A3-INTRO.text: The examiners have taken the referees' desks. Answer aloud, then reveal.

OA-A3.speaker: vera
OA-A3.text: What changed during the research, and was the question changed to fit the answer?

TPQ-ch3.speaker: marigold
TPQ-ch3.text: That second coding did not sustain two of the claim's clauses, brand and size, and produced two regularities the claim had not named, overlap and the boundary of sharing; the codebook of Table 3.5 was rewritten from its results.

FM-ASK-A3.speaker: marigold
FM-ASK-A3.text: Which two ideas got red cards, and which two came on instead?

RADIO-A3-IN.speaker: vera
RADIO-A3-IN.text: Method Works is clanking away. Hard hats on, codebook out.

RADIO-A3-OUT.speaker: vera
RADIO-A3-OUT.text: Full time at Method Works. The whistles have spoken.

EQ-ch3-eq1.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch3-eq1.text: Why critical realism and not interpretivism or positivism?

EQ-ch3-eq2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch3-eq2.text: Only four of your twenty-six interviews speak for carriers. Isn't that thin for a thesis about carriers?

EQ-ch3-eq3.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch3-eq3.text: You interviewed, coded first and wrote the claim. How do you guard against your own expectations?

EQ-ch3-eq4.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch3-eq4.text: Why raw agreement for the transcripts and Krippendorff's alpha for the arrangements?

EQ-ch3-eq5.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch3-eq5.text: Your survey asks about the four pillars, not your links. Why include it?

EQ-ch3-eq6.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch3-eq6.text: What changed during the research, and was the question changed to fit the answer?

QZ-ch3-q1.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch3-q1.text: What mode of inference does the thesis use?

QZ-ch3-q2.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch3-q2.text: What was the median length of the interviews?

QZ-ch3-q3.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch3-q3.text: How many of the 130 stances did the two readings of the third coding agree on?

QZ-ch3-q4.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch3-q4.text: Which two clauses of the working claim did the second coding not sustain?

QZ-ch3-q5.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch3-q5.text: At what consistency is a condition reported as necessary in the qualitative comparative analysis?

QZ-ch3-q6.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch3-q6.text: How many locker networks did the systematised review find?

QZ-ch3-q7.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch3-q7.text: How many usable survey responses were there?

QZ-ch3-q8.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch3-q8.text: Which of the five changes in Table 3.8 was a change of the proposed answer rather than of instrument?

KF-ch3-01.speaker: marigold
KF-ch3-01.text: Who was heard: thirty people in twenty-six interviews, by kind of party.

KF-ch3-02.speaker: marigold
KF-ch3-02.text: The instrument the School's ethics committee approved on 22 February 2024 asked fourteen questions under seven headings; a working script of twenty-three prompts in ten stages sat beside it.

KF-ch3-03.speaker: marigold
KF-ch3-03.text: The interviews were held online between July and September 2024, all conducted by the author in English.

KF-ch3-04.speaker: marigold
KF-ch3-04.text: Over the twenty-six transcripts, the two readings of the third coding gave the same stance on most concepts.

KF-ch3-05.speaker: marigold
KF-ch3-05.text: The second coding did not sustain two clauses of the working claim, brand and size, and produced two regularities the claim had not named, overlap and the boundary of sharing.

KF-ch3-06.speaker: marigold
KF-ch3-06.text: Brand, raised by the interviewer, was declined every time, and is counted as declined, not as absent.

KF-ch3-07.speaker: marigold
KF-ch3-07.text: The 117 rows of Appendix H: one row per description of an arrangement, so a count of rows is a count of accounts, not of arrangements.

KF-ch3-08.speaker: marigold
KF-ch3-08.text: The binder of each row was assigned once and carries no agreement figure; the initiator was re-checked in both passes of October 2026.

KF-ch3-09.speaker: marigold
KF-ch3-09.text: Agreement on the version 3 codes of the 117 arrangements (Krippendorff's alpha; .800 is the bar for firm conclusions).

KF-ch3-10.speaker: marigold
KF-ch3-10.text: In the crisp-set qualitative comparative analysis, a combination is taken as sufficient at a consistency of 0.8 and a condition as necessary at 0.9.

KF-ch3-11.speaker: marigold
KF-ch3-11.text: Two Ghent documents were read, both in Dutch: the draft circulation plan for the inner city and the Plan stedelijke logistiek.

KF-ch3-12.speaker: marigold
KF-ch3-12.text: The locker networks: each owner coded twice, independently, as neutral or by the kind of rival that holds the network.

KF-ch3-13.speaker: marigold
KF-ch3-13.text: The scenario costs the rule for one notional council area, as a scenario and not a forecast, counting only the increment over redirection that already happens.

KF-ch3-14.speaker: marigold
KF-ch3-14.text: The survey form recorded 132 responses between 22 February 2024 and 30 April 2025; six said No to consent and seven answered nothing more.

CN-A4-1.speaker: marigold
CN-A4-1.text: Chapter four. Witness Court. The interviews take the stand, and your old idea stands trial.

CN-A4-2.speaker: marigold
CN-A4-2.text: Every count here is a count of transcripts, and each account of an arrangement is a row: a count of accounts, not of arrangements.

CN-A4-3.speaker: marigold
CN-A4-3.text: In the dock, the Big Fierce Animal revs its engine. The charge: standing alone because it is big.

CN-A4-4.speaker: marigold
CN-A4-4.text: In the mirrors, the same firm says yes in one place and no in the next.

CN-A4-5.speaker: marigold
CN-A4-5.text: And at the back, a telephone. Head Office: never in the room, always on the line.

CN-A4-6.speaker: marigold
CN-A4-6.text: Manny Docks has the ledger: every arrangement described, and what held it together. She trusts paper over a handshake.

CN-A4-7.speaker: marigold
CN-A4-7.text: Everyone talks about trust. Watch what actually holds each arrangement together, and where it comes from.

CN-A4-8.speaker: marigold
CN-A4-8.text: In the gallery, the reader from the library has found a seat. Pen ready.

CN-A4-9.speaker: marigold
CN-A4-9.text: Your job in Witness Court: the mirror pairs, the veto above the room, what binds, and who sets the hours.

CN-A4-T1.speaker: marigold
CN-A4-T1.text: All rise. The court has heard both halves of the interviews.

CN-A4-T2.speaker: marigold
CN-A4-T2.text: Size does not sort willingness. Overlap does, unless a wall, a penalty or an owner with no stake outweighs the exposure.

CN-K4-LINKS.speaker: marigold
CN-K4-LINKS.text: Overlap. The boundary of sharing. The binder. Power.

CN-K4.speaker: marigold
CN-K4.text: Witness Court is coloured in, and the chain is lighting. Here is the court's line, word for word.

CN-K4-NEXT.speaker: marigold
CN-K4-NEXT.text: Next time: the Receiver's Clock, Ghent's gate, and a market full of lockers.

CA-K4-MANNY.speaker: manny
CA-K4-MANNY.text: Court adjourned. The ledger stays open at the Depot.

CA-K4-ANIMAL.speaker: animal
CA-K4-ANIMAL.text: Ordinary size now. Still don't want rivals on my street.

F-cutscenes-5-shots-0.speaker: marigold
F-cutscenes-5-shots-0.text: A covenant of firms, signed on trust. One action point: share data.

F-cutscenes-5-shots-1.speaker: marigold
F-cutscenes-5-shots-1.text: Years on: no data. Nothing outside held them to it.

F-cutscenes-5-shots-2.speaker: marigold
F-cutscenes-5-shots-2.text: Where a grant held them, four ended with their grant.

F-cutscenes-5-shots-3.speaker: marigold
F-cutscenes-5-shots-3.text: Proposition P3: a collaboration lasts as long as the external arrangement that binds it.

VR-ch4-tp.speaker: marigold
VR-ch4-tp.text: Counted across both halves, size does not sort willingness.

SC-4.1-L01.speaker: manny
SC-4.1-L01.text: Exhibit one: mirror pairs. The same firm, or kind of firm, giving both answers.

SC-4.1-L02.speaker: animal
SC-4.1-L02.text: Size is the whole point. I'm big, so I stand alone.

SC-4.1-L03.speaker: manny
SC-4.1-L03.text: You swap parcels across a border and refuse at home. Same size both times.

SC-4.1-FR.speaker: manny
SC-4.1-FR.text: Count the reflections in the mirror hall. Every one.

CARD-g-Mirror_pairs.speaker: marigold
CARD-g-Mirror_pairs.text: Mirror pairs. The cases in which the same firm, or the same kind of firm, said yes and no in the same breath, one answer for each side of the line.

SC-4.2-L01.speaker: manny
SC-4.2-L01.text: Local managers see the saving and say yes.

SC-4.2-L04.speaker: manny
SC-4.2-L04.text: Once it even ordered its logos seen in the city.

SC-4.2-L06.speaker: manny
SC-4.2-L06.text: So what does work? A scholar of the field put it plainly.

SC-4.2-L08.speaker: manny
SC-4.2-L08.text: Freight itself? Pooled in a handful of rows, nearly always with a binder between the parties.

SC-4.2-FR.speaker: manny
SC-4.2-FR.text: The court reporter needs the phrase the thesis is named for.

SC-4.3-L01.speaker: manny
SC-4.3-L01.text: Everyone talks about trust. My ledger says otherwise.

SC-4.3-L03.speaker: manny
SC-4.3-L03.text: Even two rival producers who pooled for years did it through a trustee. Their trust sat with the trustee, not each other.

SC-4.3-FR.speaker: manny
SC-4.3-FR.text: Ledger's open: the biggest class of binder?

CARD-g-Rule_1a.speaker: marigold
CARD-g-Rule_1a.text: Rule 1a. The codebook rule for the trustee schemes: it codes a trustee that runs a scheme as its holder and the operator it hires as a helper. Added after the results were seen; every result is reported with and without it.

CARD-g-Reciprocal_hostage.speaker: marigold
CARD-g-Reciprocal_hostage.text: Reciprocal hostage. An arrangement in which each party holds something of the other's (its parcels, its volumes or its access to a market) that it would forfeit by defecting; Williamson's term.

CARD-g-Gain-share.speaker: marigold
CARD-g-Gain-share.text: Gain-share. A contract that divides the saving a collaboration produces by a formula agreed in advance.

SC-4.4-L01.speaker: manny
SC-4.4-L01.text: And who started these? Cities first. Carriers third.

SC-4.4-L02.speaker: tilly
SC-4.4-L02.text: I set the window. The carrier picks a minute inside it.

SC-4.4-FR.speaker: manny
SC-4.4-FR.text: The clerk needs the name: who began the most?

TP-A4-L01.speaker: manny
TP-A4-L01.text: Witnesses: does size sort willingness? The court finds...

BA-A4-before-g-The_big_fierce_animal.speaker: marigold
BA-A4-before-g-The_big_fierce_animal.text: The big fierce animal. The author's 2022 image, used in his own way and not Colinvaux's: the large carrier stands alone because it takes everything within reach, while small operators share. The data corrected it to overlap; 6.4 keeps it as an image of territory.

BA-A4-after-ch4-tp.speaker: marigold
BA-A4-after-ch4-tp.text: Counted across both halves, size does not sort willingness.

MI-A4-I1.speaker: manny
MI-A4-I1.text: The trust defence counts its rows. How many?

MI-A4-I2.speaker: manny
MI-A4-I2.text: The covenant's clerk reads out what it produced.

MI-A4-I3.speaker: manny
MI-A4-I3.text: The brand hypothesis takes the stand. How did it fare?

MI-A4-CLAIM1.speaker: animal
MI-A4-CLAIM1.text: Size is the whole point. I'm big, so I stand alone.

MI-A4-WHY1.speaker: manny
MI-A4-WHY1.text: Same firm or kind of firm, both answers: what differs is overlap.

MI-A4-CLAIM2.speaker: animal
MI-A4-CLAIM2.text: Trust holds every partnership worth having.

MI-A4-WHY2.speaker: manny
MI-A4-WHY2.text: Most rows are bound from outside the parties.

MI-A4-CLAIM3.speaker: animal
MI-A4-CLAIM3.text: Give firms a covenant and goodwill, and the data will flow.

MI-A4-WHY3.speaker: manny
MI-A4-WHY3.text: Trust alone produced a covenant and no data.

MI-A4-CLAIM4.speaker: animal
MI-A4-CLAIM4.text: Rivals pool freight whenever the saving is big enough.

MI-A4-WHY4.speaker: manny
MI-A4-WHY4.text: Freight pooled in few rows, nearly always with a binder.

MI-A4-CLAIM5.speaker: animal
MI-A4-CLAIM5.text: Whoever convenes us will hold the shared point too.

MI-A4-WHY5.speaker: manny
MI-A4-WHY5.text: The binder is not the holder.

MI-A4-CLAIM6.speaker: animal
MI-A4-CLAIM6.text: I'm the one who decides how this city's parcels move.

MI-A4-WHY6.speaker: manny
MI-A4-WHY6.text: Nobody contradicted it: carriers do not decide how flows run.

SM-A4-I1.speaker: manny
SM-A4-I1.text: A witness counts the transcripts behind overlap.

SM-A4-I2.speaker: manny
SM-A4-I2.text: Objection! Explain rule 1a before the bench does.

SM-A4-I3.speaker: manny
SM-A4-I3.text: The trustee states city carriers' margins.

RH-A4-LEAD.speaker: marigold
RH-A4-LEAD.text: Dr Tally steps down from the bench with one question.

RH-A4-FB1.speaker: dr_tally
RH-A4-FB1.text: Firm held constant. That's the defence.

RH-A4-FB2.speaker: dr_tally
RH-A4-FB2.text: Over-concedes. The mirror pairs separate them: willing and unwilling firms at every size.

RH-A4-FB3.speaker: dr_tally
RH-A4-FB3.text: Overclaims. You record where size sits beside overlap, as in the postal operator's refusal.

RH2-A4-LEAD.speaker: marigold
RH2-A4-LEAD.text: Professor Kerbstone rises from the public gallery.

RH2-A4-FB1.speaker: prof_kerbstone
RH2-A4-FB1.text: Disclosed, reported both ways, claim cut to fit. Well done.

RH2-A4-FB2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
RH2-A4-FB2.text: Misdates it. It was added after the results were seen. Say that first.

RH2-A4-FB3.speaker: prof_kerbstone
RH2-A4-FB3.text: Wrong. Without it the holder condition falls short of the bar.

EC-A4-INTRO.speaker: marigold
EC-A4-INTRO.text: The examiners have taken the jury box. Answer aloud, then reveal.

OA-A4.speaker: vera
OA-A4.text: Links one to four: name each and say what its count shows.

TPQ-ch4.speaker: marigold
TPQ-ch4.text: Counted across both halves, size does not sort willingness.

FM-ASK-A4.speaker: marigold
FM-ASK-A4.text: Does being big decide whether a van shares?

RADIO-A4-IN.speaker: vera
RADIO-A4-IN.text: Live outside Witness Court. Big crowd, bigger Animal. Stay sharp.

RADIO-A4-OUT.speaker: vera
RADIO-A4-OUT.text: Court's out. The Animal's looking a bit smaller tonight.

EQ-ch4-eq1.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch4-eq1.text: Isn't overlap just size in disguise? Large carriers overlap with everyone.

EQ-ch4-eq2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch4-eq2.text: Tell me about the one transcript that contradicts overlap.

EQ-ch4-eq3.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch4-eq3.text: Two direct rivals pooled distribution for six years. Doesn't that refute your first link?

EQ-ch4-eq4.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch4-eq4.text: Your participants talk about trust constantly. How can you say trust doesn't bind?

EQ-ch4-eq5.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch4-eq5.text: Your holder result depends on a coding rule you added after seeing the results. Isn't that circular?

EQ-ch4-eq6.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch4-eq6.text: You raised brand yourself. Why does the visibility finding survive at all?

QZ-ch4-q1.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch4-q1.text: Which phrase, from a participant's description of what works, names the thesis?

QZ-ch4-q2.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch4-q2.text: How many mirror pairs does Table 4.2 set out?

QZ-ch4-q3.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch4-q3.text: In the third coding, how many of the 26 transcripts support overlap as the condition of refusal?

QZ-ch4-q4.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch4-q4.text: What is the largest class of binder across the 117 rows?

QZ-ch4-q5.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch4-q5.text: How many of the 117 rows rested on the parties' own trust, counting personal ties?

QZ-ch4-q6.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch4-q6.text: What had the covenant of forty companies produced on data sharing after four years?

QZ-ch4-q7.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch4-q7.text: Who began the most of the 117 arrangements?

QZ-ch4-q9.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch4-q9.text: How did the interviews answer the brand hypothesis when the interviewer put it?

QZ-ch4-q10.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch4-q10.text: According to the trustee (A4), what margins do city carriers run on?

KF-ch4-01.speaker: marigold
KF-ch4-01.text: Ten mirror pairs: the same firm, or the same kind of firm, gives both answers, and what differs is whether the parties compete for the same customers. A small cargo-bike operator refuses a better-funded rival in its own city and pilots with a smaller operator in another town.

KF-ch4-02.speaker: marigold
KF-ch4-02.text: Overlap as the condition of refusal, counted across the twenty-six transcripts (supporting, contradicting, mixed, silent).

KF-ch4-03.speaker: marigold
KF-ch4-03.text: The refusal is decided higher in the firm than the vehicle: three participants in three countries located the veto in a head office that was not in the room.

KF-ch4-04.speaker: marigold
KF-ch4-04.text: A scholar of the field described what works: platforms that share only the space and do not mix the freight. That sentence is the regularity the thesis is named for.

KF-ch4-05.speaker: marigold
KF-ch4-05.text: The boundary of sharing, counted across the twenty-six transcripts (supporting, contradicting, mixed, silent).

KF-ch4-06.speaker: marigold
KF-ch4-06.text: Data crosses the line only through a third party; freight itself is pooled in ten rows, and in nine of them a binder stands between the parties (in the tenth the participant named none).

KF-ch4-07.speaker: marigold
KF-ch4-07.text: What bound the 117 rows of Appendix H: ninety-five by something outside the parties, by class of binder.

KF-ch4-08.speaker: marigold
KF-ch4-08.text: Where trust stood alone it produced a covenant of forty companies whose one action point on data yielded none.

KF-ch4-09.speaker: marigold
KF-ch4-09.text: Of the twenty-three failed, unrealised and partly failed arrangements, eight had been asked to hold themselves, four ended with their grant and three failed on cost recovery.

KF-ch4-10.speaker: marigold
KF-ch4-10.text: Two multinational producers who are direct rivals pooled their distribution for six years under a trustee, one multilateral contract, a gain-share and a planning cell removed from both boards. What the parties called trust was placed in the trustee: they never learned how much more efficient the other was.

KF-ch4-11.speaker: marigold
KF-ch4-11.text: Coded for the holder, a wall, a penalty or thin flows reach six of the ten running rows with a holder code; with a no-stake holder added, nine of ten, which meets the 0.9 bar. Without rule 1a the count is six of seven, with or without the holder, below the bar.

KF-ch4-12.speaker: marigold
KF-ch4-12.text: The binder is not the holder: of the thirty-six rows whose first binder is a neutral third party, the shared point is held by a no-stake third party in only six.

KF-ch4-13.speaker: marigold
KF-ch4-13.text: Power: none of the twenty-six contradicted the reading that carriers do not decide how last-mile flows run. Counted by who began the 117 arrangements, cities and public bodies lead and carriers come third.

KF-ch4-14.speaker: marigold
KF-ch4-14.text: The visibility veto: the brand hypothesis was put by the interviewer in five interviews and declined in all five; raised unprompted in eight, three of them first-hand; and none who described it had seen it tested.

CN-A5-1.speaker: marigold
CN-A5-1.text: Chapter five. The second half of the question: what achieves collaboration's aims where collaboration between rivals does not?

CN-A5-2.speaker: marigold
CN-A5-2.text: Over the district looms the Receiver's Clock: the hours when receivers will take goods in. It limits any rule by hour.

CN-A5-3.speaker: marigold
CN-A5-3.text: Tilly Tolerance gives you a window. Not a minute more.

CN-A5-4.speaker: marigold
CN-A5-4.text: Ghent, the one city that writes hours into the permit itself, category by category, in law.

CN-A5-5.speaker: marigold
CN-A5-5.text: A permit at every hour, cameras at the cuts, and a fine for anyone without one.

CN-A5-6.speaker: marigold
CN-A5-6.text: And one delivery class held every hour, through every cut, for years.

CN-A5-7.speaker: marigold
CN-A5-7.text: Lotte Brug sets each Dutch sign beside its English meaning, and corrects your assumptions, gently.

CN-A5-8.speaker: marigold
CN-A5-8.text: Across town, the Locker Market: same lockers, different owners. Watch who delivers.

CN-A5-9.speaker: marigold
CN-A5-9.text: Lockie Keys asks who owns a locker before asking what is in it.

CN-A5-10.speaker: marigold
CN-A5-10.text: On the bridge, your note-taker reads the Dutch beside the English. So should you.

CN-A5-11.speaker: marigold
CN-A5-11.text: Your job here: the clock, the gate, the lockers, and Polly's tally. Let's ride.

CN-A5-T1.speaker: marigold
CN-A5-T1.text: Lotte opens the city's own model, in Dutch, with her English beside it.

CN-A5-T2.speaker: marigold
CN-A5-T2.text: Partitioned between operators, time is not shown to achieve the aims. Set by vehicle and hour, naming no operator, it survives.

CN-K5.speaker: marigold
CN-K5.text: Ghent Gate is coloured in. Here is its line, word for word.

CN-K5-NEXT.speaker: marigold
CN-K5-NEXT.text: Next time: Red Cell Square, and a locker bank that changes hands.

CA-K5-LOTTE.speaker: lotte
CA-K5-LOTTE.text: Tot ziens. That means see you soon.

CA-K5-ANIMAL.speaker: animal
CA-K5-ANIMAL.text: Same lockers, different owners. So who holds them?

VR-g-Access_rule_by_vehicle_and_hour_(ru.speaker: marigold
VR-g-Access_rule_by_vehicle_and_hour_(ru.text: Access rule by vehicle and hour (rule by vehicle and hour). A rule on which vehicles may enter at which hours, applying to every company alike; it names no operator, and survives as the penalty P.

SC-5.1-L01.speaker: tilly
SC-5.1-L01.text: My order, my window, barely any tolerance. Share a van? Not on my clock.

SC-5.1-L03.speaker: tilly
SC-5.1-L03.text: So the scope for sharing is gone before any carrier is asked.

SC-5.1-L04.speaker: tilly
SC-5.1-L04.text: Time came up in your interviews without anyone asking.

SC-5.1-L05.speaker: tilly
SC-5.1-L05.text: So what was all this collaboration for?

SC-5.1-FR.speaker: tilly
SC-5.1-FR.text: That's my bell. Who set the time?

CARD-g-The_receiver's_clock.speaker: marigold
CARD-g-The_receiver's_clock.text: The receiver's clock. The hours when receivers will take goods in; the limit on any rule by hour.

SC-5.2-L01.speaker: lotte
SC-5.2-L01.text: Welcome to Ghent. A permit at every hour, cameras and a fine.

SC-5.2-L02.speaker: lotte
SC-5.2-L02.text: Fewer permit categories, and all but one open around the clock.

SC-5.2-L04.speaker: lotte
SC-5.2-L04.text: And one class, sustainable urban distribution, held every hour and every cut for years.

SC-5.2-FR.speaker: lotte
SC-5.2-FR.text: A van slips through the cut at midnight. Which permit?

SC-5.3-L01.speaker: lockie
SC-5.3-L01.text: Same lockers, different owners. So who delivers?

SC-5.3-L02.speaker: lockie
SC-5.3-L02.text: Held by a firm that sells no delivery: about twice the share of main carriers that rival-held ones reach.

SC-5.3-L04.speaker: lockie
SC-5.3-L04.text: Class by class, the share falls in the order the holder's stake predicts. Too few to test.

SC-5.3-L05.speaker: lockie
SC-5.3-L05.text: And networks change hands. No rule looked again.

SC-5.3-FR.speaker: lockie
SC-5.3-FR.text: Check my tally board: the neutral-held share?

SC-5.4-L01.speaker: polly
SC-5.4-L01.text: A third of my respondents collaborate now, and the share rises with company size.

SC-5.4-L03.speaker: polly
SC-5.4-L03.text: Trust? Rated high, nobody low. Ask how they keep it, and contracts and third parties turn up.

SC-5.4-FR.speaker: polly
SC-5.4-FR.text: Last question on my list: which goal came bottom?

TP-A5-L01.speaker: lotte
TP-A5-L01.text: Your first idea: hours handed to named companies. This line from the city's own model undid it.

TP-A5-L03.speaker: lotte
TP-A5-L03.text: And later the city announced the end of the privilege.

BA-A5-before-ch5-05.speaker: marigold
BA-A5-before-ch5-05.text: 'Duurzame stadsdistributie', sustainable urban distribution, was the one delivery category with access at every hour, in every car-free area and through the three camera-controlled cuts. It was held for six years, and by 2023 it was conditional on membership, pilot projects and principles that included data sharing.

BA-A5-after-ch5-07.speaker: marigold
BA-A5-after-ch5-07.text: In 2023 Ghent announced the end of the privilege for a few partners in favour of a general rule by vehicle and hour.

MI-A5-I1.speaker: lotte
MI-A5-I1.text: My permit desk: how many categories, before and after?

MI-A5-I3.speaker: lotte
MI-A5-I3.text: Tilly's checking the open window. What did the model expect?

MI-A5-I4.speaker: lotte
MI-A5-I4.text: Polly's tally: how many rated trust highly?

SM-A5-I1.speaker: lotte
SM-A5-I1.text: A street sign shows the date the plan took effect.

SM-A5-I2.speaker: lotte
SM-A5-I2.text: Polly's other column: the biggest challenge?

SM-A5-I3.speaker: lotte
SM-A5-I3.text: Lotte counts the objections waiting for the next district.

RH-A5-LEAD.speaker: marigold
RH-A5-LEAD.text: Dr Tally is inspecting a locker door. She turns.

RH-A5-FB1.speaker: dr_tally
RH-A5-FB1.text: Difference shown, cause left to the re-reading. Exactly.

RH-A5-FB2.speaker: dr_tally
RH-A5-FB2.text: Claims cause. Significance shows a difference, not its cause. The networks were not matched.

RH-A5-FB3.speaker: dr_tally
RH-A5-FB3.text: Claims what wasn't measured. Price, size and quality were not in the data.

RH2-A5-LEAD.speaker: marigold
RH2-A5-LEAD.text: Professor Kerbstone has borrowed Polly's clipboard.

RH2-A5-FB1.speaker: prof_kerbstone
RH2-A5-FB1.text: Different measure, overlap never asked. That's the answer.

RH2-A5-FB2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
RH2-A5-FB2.text: Over-concedes. The survey measures collaborating at all, not refusing a rival.

RH2-A5-FB3.speaker: prof_kerbstone
RH2-A5-FB3.text: Claims what wasn't asked. The survey never asked about overlap, so it can't separate the two.

EC-A5-INTRO.speaker: marigold
EC-A5-INTRO.text: The examiners are sheltering under the camera gantry. Answer aloud, then reveal.

OA-A5.speaker: vera
OA-A5.text: If allocating time failed, why does time survive at all?

TPQ-ch5.speaker: marigold
TPQ-ch5.text: 'The traffic attributable to suppliers remains the same size in this time window' (p. 112).

FM-ASK-A5.speaker: marigold
FM-ASK-A5.text: What kind of rule treats every company alike?

RADIO-A5-IN.speaker: vera
RADIO-A5-IN.text: Ghent Gate, and the clock is ticking. Every window counts.

RADIO-A5-OUT.speaker: vera
RADIO-A5-OUT.text: Gate's open and the clock's happy. Tot ziens, as Lotte says.

EQ-ch5-eq1.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch5-eq1.text: Why Ghent? One city is thin evidence for a rule.

EQ-ch5-eq2.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch5-eq2.text: The locker difference could be price, size or quality. How do you know it's the holder?

EQ-ch5-eq3.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch5-eq3.text: Your survey respondents rate trust very highly. Doesn't that contradict your binder finding?

EQ-ch5-eq4.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch5-eq4.text: In the survey larger companies collaborate more. Doesn't that cut against your finding that size does not predict the refusal?

EQ-ch5-eq5.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch5-eq5.text: If allocating time failed, why does time survive at all?

QZ-ch5-q1.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch5-q1.text: When did Ghent's circulation plan take effect?

QZ-ch5-q2.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch5-q2.text: How many permit categories did the 2016 plan replace, and with how many?

QZ-ch5-q3.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch5-q3.text: Which single permit category is windowed in Ghent's 2016 regime?

QZ-ch5-q4.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch5-q4.text: What did Ghent's own 2016 model expect of the suppliers' traffic in the 18:00 to 11:00 window?

QZ-ch5-q5.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch5-q5.text: Which permit category could pass the three camera-controlled cuts at every hour?

QZ-ch5-q6.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch5-q6.text: On average, what share of a country's main carriers deliver into a locker network held by a firm that sells no delivery?

QZ-ch5-q7.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch5-q7.text: How many of the 119 survey respondents rated trust at 4 or 5?

QZ-ch5-q8.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch5-q8.text: Which goal of collaboration did the fewest survey respondents name?

QZ-ch5-q9.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch5-q9.text: Which challenge did the most survey respondents name?

QZ-ch5-q10.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch5-q10.text: How many objections to the fifth link does 5.4 line up for Chapter 6 to answer?

KF-ch5-01.speaker: marigold
KF-ch5-01.text: Sub-objective 5A: the record gives four aims attributed to collaboration, and each instrument in Chapter 5 is read against them.

KF-ch5-02.speaker: marigold
KF-ch5-02.text: Time was raised unprompted: in the third coding seven of the twenty-six transcripts speak to it, none against.

KF-ch5-03.speaker: marigold
KF-ch5-03.text: Ghent's draft circulation plan of 24 October 2016 took effect on 3 April 2017. It abolished the free window and made a permit necessary at every hour, enforced by cameras and a fine.

KF-ch5-04.speaker: marigold
KF-ch5-04.text: The 2016 plan replaced the overlapping permit categories with fewer and gave all but one access around the clock. Only loading and unloading is windowed.

KF-ch5-05.speaker: marigold
KF-ch5-05.text: 'Duurzame stadsdistributie', sustainable urban distribution, was the one delivery category with access at every hour, in every car-free area and through the three camera-controlled cuts. It was held for six years, and by 2023 it was conditional on membership, pilot projects and principles that included data sharing.

KF-ch5-06.speaker: marigold
KF-ch5-06.text: The city's own 2016 model expected delivery traffic to leave the closed hours, and expected no fall in the suppliers' traffic in the open window.

KF-ch5-07.speaker: marigold
KF-ch5-07.text: In 2023 Ghent announced the end of the privilege for a few partners in favour of a general rule by vehicle and hour.

KF-ch5-08.speaker: marigold
KF-ch5-08.text: The locker test: across the open networks, neutral-held ones reach on average about twice the share of a country's main carriers that rival-held ones do. The permutation test, which counts each ownership period once, is the result the thesis rests on.

KF-ch5-09.speaker: marigold
KF-ch5-09.text: By owner class the share of main carriers falls in an order consistent with a gradient of market commonality, though the classes are too small to test it.

KF-ch5-10.speaker: marigold
KF-ch5-10.text: Holding the carrier fixed: the same-carrier check gives the direction and does not prove it.

KF-ch5-11.speaker: marigold
KF-ch5-11.text: Three changes of holder bear on the re-check: GLS ended its cooperation after Austrian Post took over a telecoms operator's parcel stations; De Buren passed to DHL Group; myflexbox was sold to Deutsche Post, the baseline for reading the network again.

KF-ch5-12.speaker: marigold
KF-ch5-12.text: Survey: a third of those who answered collaborate horizontally now, and the share rises with company size; the survey cannot tell whether size or overlap stands behind it.

KF-ch5-13.speaker: marigold
KF-ch5-13.text: Survey: trust is rated highly, while the means named for keeping it include devices that do not rest on goodwill.

KF-ch5-14.speaker: marigold
KF-ch5-14.text: Survey: cost leads the goals; competitive advantage, the term the registration and the thesis's title carry, is named least.

CN-A6-1.speaker: marigold
CN-A6-1.text: Chapter six. The answer to the question, and a rule with no nucleus.

CN-A6-2.speaker: marigold
CN-A6-2.text: A locker bank held by a firm that sells no delivery. Rivals deliver side by side.

CN-A6-3.speaker: marigold
CN-A6-3.text: Then it is sold to a carrier.

CN-A6-4.speaker: marigold
CN-A6-4.text: The rules ask who may use it, not who holds it. None looked again.

CN-A6-5.speaker: marigold
CN-A6-5.text: Red Cell Square. The kiosk has no logo, no nucleus, and no stake in anyone's customers.

CN-A6-6.speaker: marigold
CN-A6-6.text: Corra Puscle keeps the keys. She sells no delivery, and is proud of it.

CN-A6-7.speaker: marigold
CN-A6-7.text: On Penny Slate's scale: the saving and the penalty for staying out, against the exposure and the cost of the wall.

CN-A6-8.speaker: marigold
CN-A6-8.text: Penny shows every formula, including the ones that lose money.

CN-A6-9.speaker: marigold
CN-A6-9.text: And the Big Fierce Animal is back: smaller now, still armoured, fierce on its own street.

CN-A6-10.speaker: marigold
CN-A6-10.text: Across the square, your reader underlines one word, twice. You can guess it: proposed.

CN-A6-11.speaker: marigold
CN-A6-11.text: Your job in Red Cell Square: the paradox and its mirror, the rule with no nucleus, and lawful, and fierce.

CN-A6-T1.speaker: marigold
CN-A6-T1.text: Here the overlap paradox meets its mirror. Watch the heaviest pan.

CN-A6-T2.speaker: marigold
CN-A6-T2.text: In the paradox zone, a point held by a party with no stake keeps the exposure at the display alone.

CN-A6-T3.speaker: marigold
CN-A6-T3.text: And so the fifth link lights, hollow. Proposed, not found.

CN-K6.speaker: marigold
CN-K6.text: Red Cell Square is coloured in. Here is its rule, word for word.

CN-K6-NEXT.speaker: marigold
CN-K6-NEXT.text: Next time: the Rooftops, where the question gets its answer.

CA-K6-CORRA.speaker: corra
CA-K6-CORRA.text: Look again whenever the keys change hands.

CA-K6-ANIMAL.speaker: animal
CA-K6-ANIMAL.text: So it's my street that makes me fierce. Not my size.

VR-g-The_red-cell_rule.speaker: marigold
VR-g-The_red-cell_rule.text: The red-cell rule. A shared parcel point should be held by a party with no stake in the customers of the carriers it serves, and looked at again whenever control of it changes, beside an access rule by vehicle and hour that names no operator.

SC-6.1-L01.speaker: corra
SC-6.1-L01.text: That's why my rule looks twice: at award, and whenever control changes.

SC-6.1-L02.speaker: corra
SC-6.1-L02.text: Remember the condition? Walls cut L, grants raise S, permits add P.

SC-6.1-L04.speaker: corra
SC-6.1-L04.text: Unless the point they meet at is held by someone like me. I sell no delivery.

SC-6.1-FR.speaker: corra
SC-6.1-FR.text: Which holder costs a carrier only the display?

CARD-g-The_core.speaker: marigold
CARD-g-The_core.text: The core. A split of the gain that no group would gain by leaving; for rivals it is empty wherever overlap costs them more in customers than pooling saves.

CARD-g-The_holder_principle.speaker: marigold
CARD-g-The_holder_principle.text: The holder principle. That the holder decides how much of a carrier's exposure is at stake.

SC-6.2-L01.speaker: corra
SC-6.2-L01.text: The rule, named after the cell that gives up its nucleus.

SC-6.2-L02.speaker: penny
SC-6.2-L02.text: Every point gets asked the same questions.

SC-6.2-L04.speaker: corra
SC-6.2-L04.text: Show a sign of a stake and you get the dot: notice, time to explain, then separation.

SC-6.2-L05.speaker: penny
SC-6.2-L05.text: And a check costs a modest sum a point a year.

SC-6.2-L06.speaker: penny
SC-6.2-L06.text: The bottom line for one council area: positive in the central case, negative in the low one.

SC-6.2-FR.speaker: corra
SC-6.2-FR.text: Someone's left a mark on a locker. What is it called?

CARD-g-The_dot.speaker: marigold
CARD-g-The_dot.text: The dot. A sign of a stake, named after the inclusion the spleen removes from a red cell.

SC-6.3-L01.speaker: nora
SC-6.3-L01.text: Ownership stays out of every permit condition. On its own land, the council buys neutrality as a service.

SC-6.3-L02.speaker: nora
SC-6.3-L02.text: The commons' design principles? Most are met here, but supplied from outside the parties.

SC-6.3-L03.speaker: animal
SC-6.3-L03.text: Fine. But I'm still fierce, aren't I?

SC-6.3-L05.speaker: nora
SC-6.3-L05.text: And your one sentence stands as a finding up to 'the street', and a proposition after it.

SC-6.3-FR.speaker: nora
SC-6.3-FR.text: The Animal wants it on the record: what makes it fierce?

TP-A6-L01.speaker: corra
TP-A6-L01.text: Watch the pairing hardest to make.

TP-A6-L03.speaker: animal
TP-A6-L03.text: So whoever holds the keys shouldn't want my customers.

BA-A6-before-g-The_overlap_paradox.speaker: marigold
BA-A6-before-g-The_overlap_paradox.text: The overlap paradox. The pairs with most to save are the ones who refuse, because where the saving peaks, the exposure peaks with it.

BA-A6-after-ch6-tp.speaker: marigold
BA-A6-after-ch6-tp.text: In the paradox zone, where saving and exposure peak together, a point held by a party with no stake keeps the exposure at the display alone, so that the pairing hardest to make between carriers becomes the easiest.

MI-A6-I1.speaker: corra
MI-A6-I1.text: Tap the kiosk. What is the rule named after?

MI-A6-I2.speaker: corra
MI-A6-I2.text: Penny's checklist has an impostor. Spot it.

MI-A6-I3.speaker: corra
MI-A6-I3.text: The council ranks its own sites. Which come first?

MI-A6-I4.speaker: corra
MI-A6-I4.text: Penny's slate, bottom line: the central case?

SM-A6-I1.speaker: penny
SM-A6-I1.text: In the condition, what do permits do?

SM-A6-I2.speaker: penny
SM-A6-I2.text: What does a check cost a point a year?

SM-A6-I3.speaker: penny
SM-A6-I3.text: Nora reads the verdict on the one sentence.

RH-A6-LEAD.speaker: marigold
RH-A6-LEAD.text: Professor Kerbstone posts a test parcel, then turns to you.

RH-A6-FB2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
RH-A6-FB2.text: Over-concedes. Neutrality here is a checkable market position, not a party the council designs.

RH-A6-FB3.speaker: prof_kerbstone
RH-A6-FB3.text: Promise, not position. A contract can record the holder's position but cannot create it.

RH2-A6-LEAD.speaker: marigold
RH2-A6-LEAD.text: Dr Tally lays a card on Penny's slate.

RH2-A6-FB1.speaker: dr_tally
RH2-A6-FB1.text: Cost of watching and the subcontracting. That's why.

RH2-A6-FB2.speaker: dr_tally
RH2-A6-FB2.text: Not the reason. It failed on the cost of watching, subcontracting, and the city's own model.

RH2-A6-FB3.speaker: dr_tally
RH2-A6-FB3.text: Backwards. Naming the operator is the part that failed; the rule by vehicle and hour survives.

EC-A6-INTRO.speaker: marigold
EC-A6-INTRO.text: The examiners are queuing at the kiosk like everyone else. Answer aloud, then reveal.

OA-A6.speaker: vera
OA-A6.text: The red-cell rule, and why it looks twice.

TPQ-ch6.speaker: marigold
TPQ-ch6.text: In the paradox zone, where saving and exposure peak together, a point held by a party with no stake keeps the exposure at the display alone, so that the pairing hardest to make between carriers becomes the easiest.

FM-ASK-A6.speaker: marigold
FM-ASK-A6.text: Why should the kiosk be held by someone who sells no deliveries?

RADIO-A6-IN.speaker: vera
RADIO-A6-IN.text: Red Cell Square is buzzing. Keys are changing hands, so watch who holds them.

RADIO-A6-OUT.speaker: vera
RADIO-A6-OUT.text: Square sorted. Who holds it? You know now.

EQ-ch6-eq1.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch6-eq1.text: Isn't the red-cell rule just the neutral fourth party the field has always reached for?

EQ-ch6-eq3.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch6-eq3.text: 'Open is not neutral' looks too strong. PostNL's opened lockers did get a carrier.

EQ-ch6-eq4.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch6-eq4.text: What does your rule actually deliver?

EQ-ch6-eq5.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-ch6-eq5.text: Why drop your original idea of giving hours to named companies?

EQ-ch6-eq6.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-ch6-eq6.text: A red blood cell? Isn't biology just decoration here?

QZ-ch6-q1.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch6-q1.text: What is the red-cell rule named after?

QZ-ch6-q2.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch6-q2.text: In the condition S + P ≥ L + W, what do permits do?

QZ-ch6-q3.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch6-q3.text: Which holder costs a carrier only the display?

QZ-ch6-q4.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch6-q4.text: Which of these is NOT one of the rule's four questions?

QZ-ch6-q6.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch6-q6.text: What does a council award first when it ranks sites on its own land?

QZ-ch6-q7.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch6-q7.text: About how much does a holder check cost a council per point per year?

QZ-ch6-q8.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch6-q8.text: In the scenario's central case, what is the net value a year?

QZ-ch6-q9.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch6-q9.text: According to 6.4, what makes the big fierce animal fierce?

QZ-ch6-q10.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch6-q10.text: How does the one sentence stand after 6.5's test?

KF-ch6-01.speaker: marigold
KF-ch6-01.text: The condition is the first finding written as an inequality, extending Yang, Dai and Ma's (2020) core condition from revenue lost to brand switching to every kind of exposure. Walls cut L, grants raise S and permits add P.

KF-ch6-02.speaker: marigold
KF-ch6-02.text: The overlap paradox: the pairs with most to save are the ones who refuse, because where S peaks, L peaks with it. Models put network profit rising as three carriers' areas move from adjacent to identical, against realistic pools' savings.

KF-ch6-03.speaker: marigold
KF-ch6-03.text: The red-cell rule: a shared parcel point should be held by a party with no stake in the customers of the carriers it serves, and looked at again whenever control of it changes, beside an access rule by vehicle and hour that names no operator. It is named after the cell that gives up its nucleus before it carries for the whole body.

KF-ch6-04.speaker: marigold
KF-ch6-04.text: The exposure at a shared point has two parts: the display (the brand visibility a carrier gives up whoever holds the point) and what the freight reveals, which grows with how far the holder sells the same service to the same customers and can see, keep or steer what passes.

KF-ch6-05.speaker: marigold
KF-ch6-05.text: Every point is asked the same four questions.

KF-ch6-06.speaker: marigold
KF-ch6-06.text: The rule's scope and two tiers: on the council's own land neutrality is bought as a service and sites are awarded by rank, neutral points first and open ones second; at points the council merely permits, it sets conditions of conduct and offers a neutral label. Private house-door boxes are out; rural areas are left to further research.

KF-ch6-07.speaker: marigold
KF-ch6-07.text: A sign of a stake is called the dot. It leads to written notice with the evidence and time to explain; then, on council land, an order to separate the point and, failing that, the site passes to the next-ranked holder, with appeal. The point stays in service throughout.

KF-ch6-08.speaker: marigold
KF-ch6-08.text: Pull completes the instrument: siting near residents and a checkout default to the nearest neutral point, with opt-out.

KF-ch6-09.speaker: marigold
KF-ch6-09.text: The law shapes the rule: a holder condition would restrict shareholding and combined activities under the Services Directive, so the rule keeps ownership out of every permit condition and buys neutrality as a service on council land, through a services concession in the EU or a lease in England.

KF-ch6-10.speaker: marigold
KF-ch6-10.text: A check costs a council a modest sum a point a year, paid by an audit charge on its leases.

KF-ch6-11.speaker: marigold
KF-ch6-11.text: The scenario for one council area of 50,000 households, central case: depot trips and residents' hours saved, carriers' redelivery saving, the cost of checking, and the net value. Eight of the thirteen inputs are assumptions.

KF-ch6-12.speaker: marigold
KF-ch6-12.text: Ostrom's design principles read against the binder classes: five of the eight are met, but from outside the parties (defined boundary, monitoring, graduated sanction, recognised right to organise, nested enterprise).

KF-ch6-13.speaker: marigold
KF-ch6-13.text: Hours allocated to named companies were taken apart: a rule that must know who is acting costs more to watch than one that bars an act whoever does it, and so much parcel delivery is subcontracted that the company on the permit is often not the company in the street.

KF-ch6-14.speaker: marigold
KF-ch6-14.text: The one sentence, tested clause by clause, stands as a finding up to 'the street' and as a proposition after it; no city has yet done what its last clause says.

CN-A7-1.text: Chapter seven. The Rooftops, where the question is answered in its own words.

CN-A7-3.speaker: marigold
CN-A7-3.text: Seven districts, coloured in. Now both halves of the answer: when collaboration succeeds, and what achieves its aims where it does not.

CN-A7-4.speaker: marigold
CN-A7-4.text: It comes down to two things: who wants the same door, and who can bind the people who do.

CN-A7-7.speaker: marigold

CN-A7-8.speaker: marigold

CN-A7-9.speaker: marigold
CN-A7-9.text: Answer the question in its own words, and the doors open.

CN-A7-10.speaker: marigold

QZ-ch7-q1.text: According to the first conceptual conclusion, willingness to collaborate is a property of what?

QZ-ch7-q2.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch7-q2.text: According to the third conceptual conclusion, durability is a property of what?

QZ-ch7-q3.speaker: marigold
QZ-ch7-q3.text: Which proposition reads: 'A horizontal collaboration lasts as long as the external arrangement that binds it'?

QZ-ch7-q5.text: Of the 19 arrangements carriers began, how many were between rivals?

QZ-ch7-q7.text: How many further studies does 7.5 set out before the fifth link's own?

KF-ch7-01.speaker: marigold
KF-ch7-01.text: Horizontal collaboration in European urban last-mile logistics succeeds under two conditions: the parties are not rivals for the customers at the doors they would serve together or, where they are, a wall, a penalty or an owner with no stake outweighs the exposure; and the arrangement is held by something that does not rest on the parties' goodwill.

KF-ch7-02.speaker: marigold
KF-ch7-02.text: It so rarely succeeds between competing carriers because carriers who serve the same doors fail the first condition, seldom supply each other with the second, being peers with no principal between them, and do not hold the power to reorganise their flows.

KF-ch7-03.speaker: marigold
KF-ch7-03.text: The answer to the second half of the question is a proposition, examined against the 117 arrangements, the locker networks and the rules, and not yet tested in a running scheme.

KF-ch7-04.speaker: marigold
KF-ch7-04.text: Three conceptual conclusions, a fourth that follows and a fifth offered: willingness is a property of a pair of markets, not of a firm; what a collaboration can pool is bounded by the customer relationship; durability is a property of the binder, not of the parties; the parties who can bind are those who hold the order and the permit; and the shared point should be held by a party with no stake and re-checked whenever it changes hands.

KF-ch7-05.speaker: marigold
KF-ch7-05.text: Of the 241 papers of the 2026 update: nine had been among the forty-nine, a tenth had been set aside at the 2023 final stage, thirteen named a shipper or receiver as initiator, eleven measured a running collaboration, and none reported a measured result from a collaboration carriers had begun among themselves.

KF-ch7-06.speaker: marigold
KF-ch7-06.text: Who begins a collaboration bears on what it can be: of the arrangements carriers began, few were between rivals and fewer operate.

KF-ch7-08.speaker: marigold
KF-ch7-08.text: The three named extensions of others' work.

KF-ch7-09.speaker: marigold
KF-ch7-09.text: Three papers are planned from the thesis.

KF-ch7-10.speaker: marigold
KF-ch7-10.text: Five propositions are offered, each relating two variables, claimed for the mechanism and not for a population, each with its falsifier (Table 7.1).

KF-ch7-11.speaker: marigold
KF-ch7-11.text: For funders: a grant is a binder and its end is the end of what it bound, so a grant should be written with the binder that will replace it.

KF-ch7-12.speaker: marigold
KF-ch7-12.text: The limits that bear most: few carrier voices; the demand side heard largely through those who work with it, with no residents, shopkeepers or employed drivers interviewed; silence counts that may be too high; and Ghent read in its documents, not its operators.

KF-ch7-13.speaker: marigold
KF-ch7-13.text: Seven further studies follow, from measuring the physical signal to testing the propositions as hypotheses in a deductive design in a market the thesis did not sample; the fifth link adds studies of its own, beginning with reading the locker networks again after the myflexbox sale.

KF-ch7-14.speaker: marigold
KF-ch7-14.text: The author's hardest decision: the claim that carriers refuse because the branded van is a signal was found in a minority of accounts, mostly second-hand and never measured, and was let go as the headline and kept as a finding.

BF-app-05.speaker: dr_tally

BQ-app-08.text: Can I see the search log for the locker networks?

BF-app-08.text: What did the two rules added after listing the networks do?
