MG-binder_initiator_coding.text: Why the binder was not coded a second time is not stated; the limit is.

MT-chain_referral-plain.speaker: sal
MT-chain_referral-plain.text: Asking each participant to name others who should be heard, and following those names. It reaches people you could not find alone, but the chain runs along each referrer's own network.

MT-chain_referral-how1.speaker: sal
MT-chain_referral-how1.text: 'Each was asked at the close whom else the research should hear, and the referrals were followed until the kinds of party were covered and the accounts had begun to repeat' (3.3). The working script's last stages include whom else to ask (3.3; Appendix A).

MT-chain_referral-how2.speaker: sal
MT-chain_referral-how2.text: The second stage of sampling 'was chain referral of the kind Biernacki and Waldorf (1981) describe' (3.3).

MT-chain_referral-how3.speaker: sal
MT-chain_referral-how3.text: Their named bias, 'that referrals run along the referrer's own network', was 'met here by starting the chains from each of the three kinds of party, in eleven countries, rather than from one' (3.3).

MT-chain_referral-how4.speaker: sal
MT-chain_referral-how4.text: The same bias is named for the survey, whose link was passed along the author's networks and those of the people it was passed to (3.6).

MT-chain_referral-why.speaker: sal
MT-chain_referral-why.text: The thesis gives the bias and the counter-measure; it does not say why chain referral was used beyond following the referrals 'until the kinds of party were covered and the accounts had begun to repeat' (3.3).

MT-chain_referral-not.speaker: sal
MT-chain_referral-not.text: The thesis names no alternative. Its own term is 'chain referral'; 'snowball' appears only in the title of Biernacki and Waldorf's paper.

MT-chain_referral-analogy.speaker: sal
MT-chain_referral-analogy.text: Finding good tradespeople by asking each one you hire who else they'd trust: you reach people no directory lists, but you stay inside their circle unless you start from several circles.

MX-chain_referral-b1.speaker: marigold
MX-chain_referral-b1.text: Each interview ended with one question: who else should this research hear?

MX-chain_referral-b2.speaker: marigold
MX-chain_referral-b2.text: Each name led to another conversation, like a chain of introductions.

MX-chain_referral-b3.speaker: marigold
MX-chain_referral-b3.text: The risk: every chain stays inside one person's circle.

MX-chain_referral-b4.speaker: marigold
MX-chain_referral-b4.text: So chains started from three kinds of party, in eleven countries.

MX-chain_referral-b5.speaker: marigold
MX-chain_referral-b5.text: They stopped when every kind was covered and accounts began to repeat.

MV-chain_referral-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-chain_referral-v1.text: Snowball samples stay inside one network. How did you deal with that?

MV-chain_referral-v1-ans.speaker: marigold
MV-chain_referral-v1-ans.text: That is the bias Biernacki and Waldorf name, that referrals run along the referrer's own network. I met it by starting the chains from each of the three kinds of party, in eleven countries, rather than from one (3.3).

MV-chain_referral-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-chain_referral-v2.text: When did you stop following referrals?

MV-chain_referral-v2-ans.speaker: marigold
MV-chain_referral-v2-ans.text: When the kinds of party were covered and the accounts had begun to repeat; that is the data saturation of 3.3, reached by kind of party and not by count (3.3).

MQ-chain_referral-q1.speaker: sal
MQ-chain_referral-q1.text: How did the thesis counter the bias of chain referral?

MQ-chain_referral-q2.speaker: sal
MQ-chain_referral-q2.text: Which other part of the research carries the same referral-chain bias?

MT-changes_and_design_audit-term.speaker: sam
MT-changes_and_design_audit-term.text: Recording what changed: Table 3.8, Maxwell's interactive model and the Rose audit

MT-changes_and_design_audit-plain.speaker: sam
MT-changes_and_design_audit-plain.text: Writing down every change to a design, with its reason, so a reader can see the design adjusted to evidence rather than being bent to a conclusion.

MT-changes_and_design_audit-how1.speaker: sam
MT-changes_and_design_audit-how1.text: Table 3.8 lists five changes: 1, the four-pillar interview guide became five-link coding (2024 to 2026); 2, the survey ran alongside the interviews, not after them (2024 to 2025); 3, the review was re-run with corrected strings (2026); 4, the 2023 full-text stage was re-run (2026); 5, the fifth link was re-specified from hours allocated between operators to the holder of the shared point beside an access rule by vehicle and hour (October 2026).

MT-changes_and_design_audit-how2.speaker: sam
MT-changes_and_design_audit-how2.text: 'None of the five was a change of question. The first four were changes of instrument, made because the instrument had shown its limit; the fifth was a change of the proposed answer, made because the first answer did not survive the tests put to it' (3.8).

MT-changes_and_design_audit-how3.speaker: sam
MT-changes_and_design_audit-how3.text: Change 5's reasons: Ghent expected no fall in suppliers' traffic in the hours its windows leave open (Stad Gent, 2016, p. 112), and 'a rule that must know who is acting costs more to watch than one that bars an act whoever does it' (Ostrom, 1990, p. 204) (Table 3.8).

MT-changes_and_design_audit-how4.speaker: sam
MT-changes_and_design_audit-how4.text: Figure 3.3 audits the design after Rose (1982), as Trafford and Leshem carry it (2008, p. 103): theory, propositions, design, fieldwork, results, with feedback from results back to propositions (3.7).

MT-changes_and_design_audit-how5.speaker: sam
MT-changes_and_design_audit-how5.text: Internal consistency (fieldwork against design) is checked before external consistency (conclusions against theory) (p. 104): the first is the work of Chapters 3 to 5, the second of Chapter 6 (3.7).

MT-changes_and_design_audit-how6.speaker: sam
MT-changes_and_design_audit-how6.text: 'The feedback arrows of Figure 3.3 are these five changes' (3.8).

MT-changes_and_design_audit-why.speaker: sam
MT-changes_and_design_audit-why.text: Trafford and Leshem 'hold that a change of plan must be explained in the thesis, and that accounting for it shows a reader how the research audited itself as it went (2008, pp. 99, 104)'; Maxwell's interactive model (2013), 'in which goals, framework, questions, methods and validity act on one another rather than following in sequence, is the form the five changes took' (3.8).

MT-changes_and_design_audit-analogy.speaker: sam
MT-changes_and_design_audit-analogy.text: A ship's log that records each change of course and the reason, so nobody can later say the ship simply drifted to where it landed.

MV-changes_and_design_audit-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-changes_and_design_audit-v1.text: What is the difference between a change of instrument and a change of answer?

MQ-changes_and_design_audit-q1.speaker: sam
MQ-changes_and_design_audit-q1.text: In the Rose audit as the thesis applies it, which is checked first?

MQ-changes_and_design_audit-q2.speaker: sam
MQ-changes_and_design_audit-q2.text: What are the feedback arrows of Figure 3.3?

MT-codebook_coding-term.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_coding-term.text: Codebook coding and the codebook of Table 3.5

MT-codebook_coding-plain.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_coding-plain.text: Coding text against a written codebook that defines each code and says exactly when a passage counts for or against it, so a second reader can apply the same rules.

MT-codebook_coding-how1.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_coding-how1.text: The second coding was 'a codebook coding of the kind Miles, Huberman and Saldaña (2014) describe' (3.4).

MT-codebook_coding-how2.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_coding-how2.text: Table 3.5, the transcript codebook, gives five concepts, each with a definition, a SUPPORTS-when rule, a CONTRADICTS-when rule and an example: overlap; the boundary of sharing; what binds; where the power sits; time (3.4).

MT-codebook_coding-how3.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_coding-how3.text: Example rules: overlap SUPPORTS when 'willingness is explained by the presence or absence of overlap' and CONTRADICTS when 'size or brand explains willingness regardless of overlap, or rivals for the same customers collaborate without a binder'; what binds CONTRADICTS when 'peer trust alone' sustains a working arrangement (Table 3.5).

MT-codebook_coding-how4.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_coding-how4.text: Terms fixed alongside it: a binder is 'whatever holds an arrangement together once it is formed and does not depend on the goodwill of the parties'; a reciprocal hostage (Williamson, 1983); a gain-share (3.4).

MT-codebook_coding-how5.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_coding-how5.text: The transcripts stay coded for time as Table 3.5 defines it, though the fifth link now rests on the holder (3.4).

MT-codebook_coding-how6.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_coding-how6.text: The 117 arrangements were coded against a second codebook, in versions 2 and 3 (Appendix L) (3.4).

MT-codebook_coding-why.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_coding-why.text: Codebook work allows the agreement check O'Connor and Joffe (2020) recommend (3.4). The second coding was a codebook coding 'made to test what the first had produced before anything was built on it' (3.4).

MT-codebook_coding-not.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_coding-not.text: Open, uncodified coding, which is what the first coding under the pillars was (3.4).

MT-codebook_coding-analogy.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_coding-analogy.text: A marking scheme for an exam: it says what earns the mark and what loses it, so two examiners can mark the same script independently.

MV-codebook_coding-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-codebook_coding-v1.text: Why are the transcripts still coded for time when the fifth link is now the holder?

MV-codebook_coding-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-codebook_coding-v2.text: What would make a transcript contradict the overlap concept?

MQ-codebook_coding-q1.speaker: sam
MQ-codebook_coding-q1.text: How many concepts does the transcript codebook of Table 3.5 hold?

MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-term.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-term.text: Codebook versions 1 to 3, the pilot, and settling disagreements

MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-plai.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-plai.text: Writing the coding rules, trying them on a few cases, revising them, then coding everything twice and resolving every disagreement against the written rules.

MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-how1.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-how1.text: Version 1 was piloted on ten rows coded independently twice; 'the two codings raised the same problems and seven changes followed', giving version 2 (3.4).

MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-how2.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-how2.text: Version 2 records for each arrangement the parties' market commonality and footprint, the stage of the chain they share, where the saving comes from, the volume of the flows, what crosses between them, the wall that keeps them apart, any penalty for staying out, and the outcome; all 117 rows coded twice, in two passes (3.4).

MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-how3.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-how3.text: In version 2 the wall counted a trustee and a helper's position among its values; version 3 'moved both to the holder of the shared point' (3.4).

MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-how4.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-how4.text: Version 3 records the class of whoever controls the point where the parties' parcels, data or customer contact meet (receiver, no-stake third party, helper, public body, rival party or joint holder), whether that holder sells delivery to the parties' customers, and whether its co-users are rivals; piloted on the same ten rows, extended by eleven rules, and coded twice over all 117, 'each pass made from Appendix H and the transcripts without sight of the earlier codes or of the other pass' (3.4).

MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-how5.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-how5.text: Settlement: 'Every disagreement was listed, the rows on which a difference changes a result were isolated, and each was settled against the codebook with its reason recorded' (3.4).

MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-how6.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-how6.text: 'Each change to the codebook is dated in Appendix L, and where a change alters a result both results are reported'; Chapter 4 reports the two versions side by side (3.4).

MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-why.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-why.text: Version 3 separates the holder from the wall 'so that a neutral third party is a binder in Table 3.5 and, where it controls the point at which the parties meet, a holder in version 3' (3.4). The pilot exists to find problems before the full coding (3.4).

MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-anal.speaker: sam
MT-codebook_versions_and_settlement-anal.text: Testing a new form on ten customers, fixing the confusing questions, then giving it to everyone, with two clerks entering each form separately and a supervisor resolving every mismatch against the instructions.

MV-codebook_versions_and_settlement-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-codebook_versions_and_settlement-v1.text: Why did you need a third version of the codebook?

MV-codebook_versions_and_settlement-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-codebook_versions_and_settlement-v2.text: How were disagreements between passes resolved?

MQ-codebook_versions_and_settlement-q1.speaker: sam
MQ-codebook_versions_and_settlement-q1.text: How many rows were used to pilot the arrangement codebook?

MQ-codebook_versions_and_settlement-q2.speaker: sam
MQ-codebook_versions_and_settlement-q2.text: What did version 3 separate from the wall?

MQ-codebook_versions_and_settlement-q3.speaker: sam
MQ-codebook_versions_and_settlement-q3.text: How many rules was version 3 extended by after its pilot?

MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-term.speaker: lockie
MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-term.text: Cohen's kappa and the survey's open answers

MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-plain.speaker: lockie
MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-plain.text: Cohen's kappa measures agreement between two codings beyond what chance would give, for categorical codes; 1.00 is perfect agreement.

MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-how1.speaker: lockie
MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-how1.text: The open question, on key factors for success, was answered by 39; answers were coded inductively (Braun and Clarke, 2006) into six themes and a code for answers with nothing of substance; an answer may carry more than one theme; the codebook is in Appendix K (3.6).

MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-how2.speaker: lockie
MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-how2.text: Coded twice, independently, against one codebook; the second coding blind, from the codebook and the answers alone (3.6).

MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-how3.speaker: lockie
MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-how3.text: 'The two codings agreed on all 39 answers (Cohen's kappa 1.00 over 273 coding decisions, seven codes for each answer; Cohen, 1960), reported as O'Connor and Joffe (2020) recommend for codebook work' (3.6).

MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-how4.speaker: lockie
MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-how4.text: Limit: 'The codebook was drawn up from these answers in the first coding, which makes agreement easier to reach in so short a set, and the agreement is reported with that limit' (3.6).

MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-how5.speaker: lockie
MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-how5.text: Themes (5.3): agreed terms and a party to hold them (10); the means and the money (9); public rules, powers or incentives (7); trust between the partners (6); customers and data stay with their owner (5); the decision placed with another party (3); six said nothing of substance.

MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-how6.speaker: lockie
MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-how6.text: The open question came last, after the items on trust, 'so its answers may echo them'; they are read 'as examples of what respondents say and not as a count of the industry's view' (5.3).

MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-why.speaker: lockie
MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-why.text: Reported as O'Connor and Joffe recommend for codebook work (3.6). The thesis does not say why kappa here rather than alpha.

MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-not.speaker: lockie
MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-not.text: Krippendorff's alpha, used for the arrangements; raw agreement, used for the transcripts (3.4).

MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-analogy.speaker: lockie
MT-cohens_kappa_open_answers-analogy.text: Two judges scoring the same thirty-nine entries against a rubric one of them helped write: perfect agreement is good, but expected.

MV-cohens_kappa_open_answers-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-cohens_kappa_open_answers-v1.text: A kappa of 1.00 looks too perfect.

MV-cohens_kappa_open_answers-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-cohens_kappa_open_answers-v2.text: What did the open answers say?

MQ-cohens_kappa_open_answers-q1.speaker: lockie
MQ-cohens_kappa_open_answers-q1.text: Over how many coding decisions was kappa computed?

MQ-cohens_kappa_open_answers-q2.speaker: lockie
MQ-cohens_kappa_open_answers-q2.text: Which theme was largest in the open answers?

MG-cohens_kappa_open_answers.speaker: lockie
MG-cohens_kappa_open_answers.text: Why kappa rather than alpha for the open answers is not stated.

MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-term.speaker: sam
MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-term.text: The comparator interview and out-of-domain transcripts kept in the denominator

MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-plain.speaker: sam
MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-plain.text: A comparator is a case from outside the main boundary, kept to contrast with the rest. Out-of-domain transcripts are interviews that turned out to be about something else; keeping them in the count avoids quietly improving the numbers.

MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-how1.speaker: sam
MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-how1.text: One interview 'was held as a comparator from outside Europe; it stands, like every transcript, in each count of twenty-six, contributes three rows to Appendix H, read as comparators, and is drawn on only where the text says so' (3.3; 1.4).

MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-how2.speaker: sam
MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-how2.text: Two transcripts, B10 (an engineer on interurban weight enforcement) and B11 (a site host who had 'not really' looked at logistics), 'proved on reading to lie outside the domain' (3.7; 4.1).

MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-how3.speaker: sam
MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-how3.text: They are kept in the set and in Table 3.4; both codings record them as silent on most concepts; they stand in every denominator of twenty-six; their eight rows stand in the 117; 'no finding in Chapters 4 and 5 rests on them alone' (3.7).

MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-how4.speaker: sam
MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-how4.text: Table 4.1 flags every transcript's quality: for example A2 'not specifically urban', A5 eight minutes of prepared answers, A9 typed answers, B8 the poorest recording (4.1).

MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-why.speaker: sam
MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-why.text: The thesis states the treatment but not an explicit reason for keeping out-of-domain transcripts in the denominator. Its stated rule is that no finding rests on them alone (3.7).

MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-not.speaker: sam
MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-not.text: Dropping them from the count is not done, and the thesis does not discuss it.

MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-analogy.speaker: sam
MT-comparator_and_out_of_domain-analogy.text: Keeping the two jurors who slept through a trial in the headcount, and saying so, rather than reporting a unanimous verdict from ten.

MV-comparator_and_out_of_domain-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-comparator_and_out_of_domain-v1.text: Why keep two out-of-domain interviews in your denominator of twenty-six?

MV-comparator_and_out_of_domain-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-comparator_and_out_of_domain-v2.text: Why is there an Indian interview in a European thesis?

MQ-comparator_and_out_of_domain-q1.speaker: sam
MQ-comparator_and_out_of_domain-q1.text: Which two transcripts lie outside the domain?

MQ-comparator_and_out_of_domain-q2.speaker: sam
MQ-comparator_and_out_of_domain-q2.text: How many rows of Appendix H do the two out-of-domain transcripts contribute?

MG-comparator_and_out_of_domain.speaker: sam
MG-comparator_and_out_of_domain.text: The reason for keeping out-of-domain transcripts in the denominator is implied, not stated. Say it plainly if asked.

MT-comparing_unlike_sets-term.speaker: ada
MT-comparing_unlike_sets-term.text: Comparing the forty-nine and the 241: different kinds of count

MT-comparing_unlike_sets-plain.speaker: ada
MT-comparing_unlike_sets-plain.text: Two sets of papers that passed different tests cannot be compared as if they were equal; every comparison has to say which test each set passed.

MT-comparing_unlike_sets-how1.speaker: ada
MT-comparing_unlike_sets-how1.text: 'The forty-nine of 2023 are papers included after full-text reading, while the 241 of 2026 are papers retained after title-and-abstract screening and the citation rule, of which a hundred and seventy were read in full; wherever the two figures stand together in this thesis the text says which kind each is' (3.2).

MT-comparing_unlike_sets-how2.speaker: ada
MT-comparing_unlike_sets-how2.text: 'The comparisons that follow set a stricter set beside a looser one' (2.2).

MT-comparing_unlike_sets-how3.speaker: ada
MT-comparing_unlike_sets-how3.text: By type: over half the 241 (124) are models or simulations, against a third of the forty-nine; reviews fall from a quarter to an eighth; empirical studies (56 in the 241) hold at about a fifth in both (2.2).

MT-comparing_unlike_sets-how4.speaker: ada
MT-comparing_unlike_sets-how4.text: No initiator named: 128 of the 241 (53 per cent), against 23 of the forty-nine (47 per cent) counted the same way (2.2).

MT-comparing_unlike_sets-how5.speaker: ada
MT-comparing_unlike_sets-how5.text: 'At least thirty-two' of the forty-nine (65 per cent) is a separate count, of papers that observe no real arrangement: it takes in ten that name a type of actor in general and leaves out Allen and colleagues (2018), who name no one but track real vans (Table 2.1 note; 2.2).

MT-comparing_unlike_sets-why.speaker: ada
MT-comparing_unlike_sets-why.text: Because the two sets passed different tests (3.2).

MT-comparing_unlike_sets-analogy.speaker: ada
MT-comparing_unlike_sets-analogy.text: Comparing pass rates when one school counts pupils who sat the exam and another counts every pupil who registered.

MV-comparing_unlike_sets-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-comparing_unlike_sets-v1.text: 'At least thirty-two' and 'twenty-three' both describe the forty-nine and the initiator. Which is right?

MV-comparing_unlike_sets-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-comparing_unlike_sets-v2.text: How do the 241 differ in kind from the forty-nine?

MQ-comparing_unlike_sets-q1.speaker: ada
MQ-comparing_unlike_sets-q1.text: What test had the 241 update papers passed?

MQ-comparing_unlike_sets-q2.speaker: ada
MQ-comparing_unlike_sets-q2.text: How many of the 241 name no initiator?

MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-term.speaker: lockie
MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-term.text: 'Consistent with, not a test of': one-time comparison versus cause

MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-plain.speaker: lockie
MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-plain.text: A difference found by comparing cases at one moment can fit an explanation without proving it; showing cause needs, for example, watching the same cases before and after a change.

MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-how1.speaker: lockie
MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-how1.text: The locker result 'is a difference between types of owner. It fits the link but does not test it' (1.5).

MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-how2.speaker: lockie
MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-how2.text: 'The test compares networks at one time: it shows a difference by owner class, and it neither measures a gradient between pairs of firms nor shows a cause' (5.2).

MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-how3.speaker: lockie
MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-how3.text: Holders are coded by class, not by their market commonality with each carrier, so the result is 'consistent with the gradient P5 proposes and not a test of it' (7.4; 3.7).

MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-how4.speaker: lockie
MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-how4.text: By owner class the share falls from 46 (neutral) to 42 (retailers with own delivery), 29 (carriers' subsidiaries), 17 (carrier-owned), 15 (postal operators) and none for the one joint network, 'an ordering consistent with a gradient of market commonality ... though the classes are too small to test it' (5.2).

MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-how5.speaker: lockie
MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-how5.text: Named threats: published sources may under-record carriers; a neutral network, which lives by selling access, may have more reason to list its carriers; the networks were not matched on price, size or terms, and no public measure of quality was found (5.2; 3.5).

MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-how6.speaker: lockie
MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-how6.text: Changes of owner are read both ways: GLS ended its cooperation after Austrian Post took over a telecoms operator's stations (by February 2024), though that may reflect the new owner's terms; De Buren passed to DHL Group in May 2025 with DPD and UPS named on the day of sale and no later statement; myflexbox's sale to Deutsche Post on 1 October 2026 is the baseline (5.2).

MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-how7.speaker: lockie
MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-how7.text: 'Cause is left to reading the networks again after each change of holder (7.5)' (5.2).

MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-why.speaker: lockie
MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-why.text: As stated in 5.2 and 7.4: a comparison at one time, by class, unmatched on quality, cannot show cause.

MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-not.speaker: lockie
MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-not.text: A before-and-after design after each change of holder, and a quality-matched comparison, both left to further research (7.5; 7.4).

MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-analogy.speaker: lockie
MT-consistent_with_not_a_test-analogy.text: Finding that towns with more fire stations have fewer house fires is consistent with stations preventing fires, but you'd need to watch towns before and after a station opens to know.

MV-consistent_with_not_a_test-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-consistent_with_not_a_test-v1.text: The locker difference could be price, size or quality. How do you know it's the holder?

MV-consistent_with_not_a_test-v1-ans.speaker: marigold
MV-consistent_with_not_a_test-v1-ans.text: I don't claim to. The test compares networks at one time, by owner class, unmatched on price, size or terms, because no public measure of quality was found. It shows a difference by owner class consistent with the proposition, and the same-carrier check gives the direction. Cause is left to reading the networks again after each change of holder, with myflexbox's sale as the baseline (5.2; 7.4; 7.5).

MV-consistent_with_not_a_test-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-consistent_with_not_a_test-v2.text: Your sales evidence cuts both ways. Why include it?

MV-consistent_with_not_a_test-v2-ans.speaker: marigold
MV-consistent_with_not_a_test-v2-ans.text: Because it is the only evidence of drift by sale, and I read each sale both ways: GLS's exit after Austrian Post's takeover may reflect the new owner's terms; De Buren shows no exit at sale but no later statement either. Two changes of owner are thin, and 3.7 says so (5.2; 3.7).

MQ-consistent_with_not_a_test-q1.speaker: lockie
MQ-consistent_with_not_a_test-q1.text: What does the locker test NOT show, according to 5.2?

MQ-consistent_with_not_a_test-q2.speaker: lockie
MQ-consistent_with_not_a_test-q2.text: Which owner class reaches the smallest share of main carriers?

MT-counting_in_qualitative-plain.speaker: manny
MT-counting_in_qualitative-plain.text: Qualitative studies can report counts to show how widely a pattern holds and where it does not, without treating the count as a statistical test.

MT-counting_in_qualitative-how1.speaker: manny
MT-counting_in_qualitative-how1.text: 'The counts are used in the way Hannah and Lautsch (2011) allow a qualitative study to count, to show how widely a pattern holds across the set and where it does not, never as a test of it, and each is tied to the file and the row it came from' (3.4).

MT-counting_in_qualitative-how2.speaker: manny
MT-counting_in_qualitative-how2.text: 'Every count in Chapters 4 and 5 comes from those files and not from memory of them' (3.4).

MT-counting_in_qualitative-how3.speaker: manny
MT-counting_in_qualitative-how3.text: Stances are counted by transcript, arrangements by row (3.4; 4.1).

MT-counting_in_qualitative-how4.speaker: manny
MT-counting_in_qualitative-how4.text: 'These are counts of rows of Appendix H, made from participants' accounts, not of measured deliveries' (4.4).

MT-counting_in_qualitative-analogy.speaker: manny
MT-counting_in_qualitative-analogy.text: A head gardener noting that blight appeared on eleven of twelve rows: a tally that shows how far the problem spread, not a laboratory trial.

MV-counting_in_qualitative-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-counting_in_qualitative-v1.text: You report counts and percentages. Isn't that quantitative?

MV-counting_in_qualitative-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-counting_in_qualitative-v2.text: How do I know a count wasn't made from memory?

MQ-counting_in_qualitative-q1.speaker: manny
MQ-counting_in_qualitative-q1.text: Whose account of counting in qualitative research does 3.4 follow?

MQ-counting_in_qualitative-q2.speaker: manny
MQ-counting_in_qualitative-q2.text: What are the counts of Appendix H rows counts of?

MT-critical_realism-plain.speaker: sal
MT-critical_realism-plain.text: The view that there is a real world of structures and causal mechanisms that exist whether or not we see them, and that our knowledge of it is fallible. Research tries to explain what produces the patterns we observe.

MT-critical_realism-how1.speaker: sal
MT-critical_realism-how1.text: Named as the paradigm in the abstract ('A critical realist, theory-building design') and first in Chapter 3 (3.1).

MT-critical_realism-how2.speaker: sal
MT-critical_realism-how2.text: Its assumptions are stated (Bhaskar, 2008; Sayer, 2000): a real world of last-mile markets whose structures (who competes with whom for which customers, who can bind whom) exist whether or not any participant describes them accurately; knowledge of it is fallible and comes through accounts, documents and numbers; explanation is retroductive (3.1).

MT-critical_realism-how3.speaker: sal
MT-critical_realism-how3.text: The refusals and the few collaborations that did work are treated 'as the visible result of deeper causes, overlap and binding, which play out differently in different settings' (3.1).

MT-critical_realism-how4.speaker: sal
MT-critical_realism-how4.text: Consequences for the design: 'the interviews were searched as carefully for evidence against the mechanism as for evidence for it'; the mechanism was tested against 'the one city that already shares out delivery hours by law', and the holder against the 117 arrangements, forty-three locker networks and the rules; and 'Chapter 2 presents the framework as coming out of the evidence rather than being laid over it' (3.1).

MT-critical_realism-how5.speaker: sal
MT-critical_realism-how5.text: 'The closest example of this approach is Easton (2010), who made the case for critical realism in research on industrial networks, the ties between firms that trade with one another, and this thesis follows him' (3.1).

MT-critical_realism-why.speaker: sal
MT-critical_realism-why.text: Three reasons, and 'each rival position fails one of them' (3.1). First, 'what needs explaining is a pattern across twenty-six accounts, a refusal to collaborate that comes back wherever the parties' customers overlap', and 'a positivist design would have needed a full list of operators to draw a sample from and a tested way to measure willingness to collaborate, and the field has neither'. Second, 'the markets, the customers and the binders exist however well or badly a participant describes them, and an interpretivist design would not make that claim'. Third, 'the explanation sought is a mechanism that can be tested against the cases that should break it, which is retroduction, not induction'. In 7.4: chosen 'because the question was about mechanisms and the evidence was accounts'. The stated cost: 'a mechanism named from twenty-six accounts is a proposition, and what it generalises to is the mechanism, which may work elsewhere, not a population' (3.1).

MT-critical_realism-not.speaker: sal
MT-critical_realism-not.text: Positivism ('no register to draw a sample from and no established measure of willingness to test') and interpretivism ('overlap and binding are held to be real, not only reported') (Table 3.2).

MT-critical_realism-analogy.speaker: sal
MT-critical_realism-analogy.text: An accident investigator treats witness statements as fallible, but assumes the brakes, the road and the weather were real, and works back to the mechanism that explains why crashes keep happening at the same bend.

MV-critical_realism-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-critical_realism-v1.text: What does critical realism let you claim that interpretivism would not?

MV-critical_realism-v1-ans.speaker: marigold
MV-critical_realism-v1-ans.text: That overlap and binding are real: the markets, the customers and the binders exist however well or badly a participant describes them. An interpretivist reading would give me credible interpretations of what collaboration means to each participant, but it would say nothing about the mechanism (3.1; Table 3.2; 7.4).

MV-critical_realism-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-critical_realism-v2.text: What does the choice cost you?

MV-critical_realism-v2-ans.speaker: marigold
MV-critical_realism-v2-ans.text: A mechanism named from twenty-six accounts is retroduced, not observed, so it is a proposition, and what it generalises to is the mechanism, which may work elsewhere, not a population. That is why Chapter 7 offers propositions with falsifiers for others to test (3.1, 3.7, 7.2).

MV-critical_realism-v3-ans.speaker: marigold
MV-critical_realism-v3-ans.text: The closest example of this approach is Easton (2010), who made the case for critical realism in research on industrial networks, and I follow him. Wynn and Williams (2012) turn the position into principles for case research, and Chapter 3 is arranged so that each principle can be pointed to (3.1).

MQ-critical_realism-q1.speaker: sal
MQ-critical_realism-q1.text: Which of these is one of the three reasons 3.1 gives for choosing critical realism?

MQ-critical_realism-q2.speaker: sal
MQ-critical_realism-q2.text: Which work does 3.1 call the closest example of this approach?

MQ-critical_realism-q3.speaker: sal
MQ-critical_realism-q3.text: In the thesis's critical realist reading, what are overlap and binding?

MT-csqca-plain.speaker: manny
MT-csqca-plain.text: A method for comparing a modest number of cases as combinations of conditions. In the crisp-set form each condition is simply present or absent, and the analysis asks which conditions, or combinations, go with an outcome.

MT-csqca-how1.speaker: manny
MT-csqca-how1.text: 'The settled codes were compared by crisp-set qualitative comparative analysis (Ragin, 1987, 2008), which asks which conditions are present wherever an outcome is, and which combinations of them are followed by it wherever they occur' (3.4).

MT-csqca-how2.speaker: manny
MT-csqca-how2.text: Thresholds 'at the conventional thresholds (Schneider and Wagemann, 2012)': a combination sufficient at a consistency of 0.8, the run repeated at 0.75 and 0.9; a condition necessary at 0.9 (3.4).

MT-csqca-how3.speaker: manny
MT-csqca-how3.text: Rows tested: rivals not far from the customer (at the last leg, at the door or at no stage named): 22 in one replication and 21 in the other; outcome: running at interview (4.4).

MT-csqca-how4.speaker: manny
MT-csqca-how4.text: With a wall or a penalty, running in 11 of 13 and 11 of 12; with neither, 3 of 8 and 2 of 8 (4.4).

MT-csqca-how5.speaker: manny
MT-csqca-how5.text: Kept to rows where something that could expose customers, brand, data or freight crossed: 7 of 8 running with a wall or penalty against 1 of 6 with neither; 8 of 9 against 1 of 7 (4.4).

MT-csqca-how6.speaker: manny
MT-csqca-how6.text: The one exception that runs: two bike couriers' joint bid (H.2 56), with no wall and no penalty (4.4).

MT-csqca-how7.speaker: manny
MT-csqca-how7.text: Appendix L lists the minimised combinations found sufficient; the main text reports the running counts and the necessity result, not those combinations.

MT-csqca-why.speaker: manny
MT-csqca-why.text: The thesis does not say why it chose QCA, or the crisp-set form, for the 117; it says what the method asks (3.4).

MT-csqca-not.speaker: manny
MT-csqca-not.text: Regression is ruled out only for the locker test ('with so few periods no regression was run', 3.5); no alternative is named for the 117.

MT-csqca-analogy.speaker: manny
MT-csqca-analogy.text: A doctor reviewing a ward's charts as yes/no ticks (smoker, diabetic, over sixty) to see which ticks appear in every patient who recovered.

MX-csqca-b1.speaker: marigold
MX-csqca-b1.text: QCA compares cases as combinations of conditions.

MX-csqca-b2.speaker: marigold
MX-csqca-b2.text: Crisp-set means each condition is simply on or off.

MX-csqca-b3.speaker: marigold
MX-csqca-b3.text: First question: which conditions are on wherever the outcome is?

MX-csqca-b4.speaker: marigold
MX-csqca-b4.text: Second: which combinations are followed by the outcome wherever they occur?

MX-csqca-b5.speaker: marigold
MX-csqca-b5.text: Here the outcome is 'running at interview', among rivals close to the customer.

MX-csqca-b6.speaker: marigold
MX-csqca-b6.text: Thresholds: 0.8 for sufficiency, 0.9 for necessity. Each case dropped in turn to check.

MV-csqca-v1-ans.speaker: marigold
MV-csqca-v1-ans.text: QCA asks which conditions are present wherever an outcome is, and which combinations are followed by it wherever they occur, which is the shape of my question about the arrangements: what is there whenever rivals near the customer keep running. The thesis states what the method asks and its conventional thresholds; it doesn't argue QCA against other methods (3.4).

MV-csqca-v2-ans.speaker: marigold
MV-csqca-v2-ans.text: They are listed in Appendix L. In the main text I report the running counts, eleven of thirteen and eleven of twelve with a wall or a penalty against three of eight and two of eight with neither, and the necessity result (4.4; Appendix L).

MV-csqca-v3.speaker: dr_tally
MV-csqca-v3.text: What is the outcome in your QCA?

MV-csqca-v3-ans.speaker: marigold
MV-csqca-v3-ans.text: Whether the arrangement was running at interview, among rows between rivals not far from the customer: twenty-two rows in one replication, twenty-one in the other (4.4).

MQ-csqca-q1.speaker: manny
MQ-csqca-q1.text: What two questions does crisp-set QCA ask, as 3.4 puts it?

MQ-csqca-q2.speaker: manny
MQ-csqca-q2.text: Among rivals not far from the customer with a wall or a penalty, how many arrangements were running in one replication?

MG-csqca.speaker: manny
MG-csqca.text: Why QCA, and why crisp-set, are not argued; the sufficient combinations appear only in Appendix L.

MT-decision_rule_power-term.speaker: ada
MT-decision_rule_power-term.text: The decision rule on power in the update

MT-decision_rule_power-plain.speaker: ada
MT-decision_rule_power-plain.text: A decision rule is a stated rule for turning what a source says into a count. If the rule assumes the claim being tested, that count cannot test the claim.

MT-decision_rule_power-how1.speaker: ada
MT-decision_rule_power-how1.text: Two rules turned card stances into counts, each for a stated reason (2.2).

MT-decision_rule_power-how2.speaker: ada
MT-decision_rule_power-how2.text: First: a card marked 'not in text' counts as silent.

MT-decision_rule_power-how3.speaker: ada
MT-decision_rule_power-how3.text: Second, on power: the cards name who a paper treats as deciding and do not state a stance, so a paper naming shippers, receivers, cities or a neutral orchestrator was counted as support, and one naming carriers as against (2.2).

MT-decision_rule_power-how4.speaker: ada
MT-decision_rule_power-how4.text: A neutral orchestrator is 'a party that sells neither delivery nor the parties' kind of goods to their customers' (2.2).

MT-decision_rule_power-how5.speaker: ada
MT-decision_rule_power-how5.text: Thirty-eight of the 241 verdicts on power rest on that rule (2.2).

MT-decision_rule_power-how6.speaker: ada
MT-decision_rule_power-how6.text: 'That rule assumes the thesis's own claim, so this count cannot test it. It shows only whom the field assumes decides.' Power is tested in 4.5, on the interviews and on who began the 117 arrangements (2.2).

MT-decision_rule_power-why.speaker: ada
MT-decision_rule_power-why.text: Because the cards 'name who a paper treats as deciding and do not state a stance' (2.2).

MT-decision_rule_power-not.speaker: ada
MT-decision_rule_power-not.text: The thesis names no alternative rule.

MT-decision_rule_power-analogy.speaker: ada
MT-decision_rule_power-analogy.text: Judging a cookery contest by counting how often the judges mention your recipe: it tells you what they talk about, not whether you won.

MV-decision_rule_power-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-decision_rule_power-v1.text: How many power verdicts rest on the rule, and what follows?

MV-decision_rule_power-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-decision_rule_power-v2.text: Why did you need a rule at all?

MQ-decision_rule_power-q1.speaker: ada
MQ-decision_rule_power-q1.text: How many of the 241 verdicts on power rest on the decision rule?

MQ-decision_rule_power-q2.speaker: ada
MQ-decision_rule_power-q2.text: Where is the power link actually tested?

MT-deduction_and_induction-plain.speaker: sam
MT-deduction_and_induction-plain.text: Deduction starts from a theory and tests its predictions against data. Induction starts from the data and builds general statements up from it.

MT-deduction_and_induction-how1.speaker: sam
MT-deduction_and_induction-how1.text: Table 3.2 assigns deduction to positivism ('hypotheses tested against measurement') and induction to interpretivism ('accounts built up from what participants say').

MT-deduction_and_induction-how2.speaker: sam
MT-deduction_and_induction-how2.text: Stage one, the 2022-23 systematic review, was 'deductive under the four pillars of the registration: trust, efficiency, innovation, sustainability' (3.1).

MT-deduction_and_induction-how3.speaker: sam
MT-deduction_and_induction-how3.text: Stage two, the interviews, were 'read inductively and coded three times' (3.1).

MT-deduction_and_induction-how4.speaker: sam
MT-deduction_and_induction-how4.text: The survey's open answers were 'coded inductively, in the manner Braun and Clarke (2006) describe' (3.6).

MT-deduction_and_induction-how5.speaker: sam
MT-deduction_and_induction-how5.text: The overall mode is retroduction, 'not induction' (3.1).

MT-deduction_and_induction-how6.speaker: sam
MT-deduction_and_induction-how6.text: The seventh further study would 'test the propositions of 7.2 as hypotheses in a deductive design in a market this thesis did not sample' (7.5).

MT-deduction_and_induction-why.speaker: sam
MT-deduction_and_induction-why.text: For the overall mode, see retroduction (3.1). The thesis does not say why the 2023 review was run deductively under the four pillars, beyond their being the pillars of the registration.

MT-deduction_and_induction-not.speaker: sam
MT-deduction_and_induction-not.text: Neither is the overall mode; the thesis adopts retroduction.

MT-deduction_and_induction-analogy.speaker: sam
MT-deduction_and_induction-analogy.text: Deduction is checking yesterday's forecast against today's sky; induction is keeping a diary of skies until a pattern shows.

MV-deduction_and_induction-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-deduction_and_induction-v1.text: Where in the research is there deduction, and where induction?

MV-deduction_and_induction-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-deduction_and_induction-v2.text: If the interviews were read inductively, why is your framework not simply inductive?

MQ-deduction_and_induction-q1.speaker: sam
MQ-deduction_and_induction-q1.text: Under which framework was the 2023 systematic review deductive?

MQ-deduction_and_induction-q2.speaker: sam
MQ-deduction_and_induction-q2.text: What does 7.5 propose as the seventh further study?

MG-deduction_and_induction.speaker: sam
MG-deduction_and_induction.text: Why the 2023 review was deductive under the pillars is not argued.

MT-descriptive_analysis-term.speaker: lockie
MT-descriptive_analysis-term.text: Descriptive analysis only: counts, percentages and cross-tabulations

MT-descriptive_analysis-plain.speaker: lockie
MT-descriptive_analysis-plain.text: Describing what respondents said with counts, percentages and two-way tables, without statistical tests or claims about a wider population.

MT-descriptive_analysis-how1.speaker: lockie
MT-descriptive_analysis-how1.text: 'The analysis is descriptive: counts, percentages of those who answered each item, and cross-tabulations by company size and by whether the company collaborates now' (3.6).

MT-descriptive_analysis-how2.speaker: lockie
MT-descriptive_analysis-how2.text: Percentages are whole numbers in the chapters and to one decimal place in Appendix K (3.6).

MT-descriptive_analysis-how3.speaker: lockie
MT-descriptive_analysis-how3.text: 'No test of significance is run and nothing is inferred to a population' (3.6).

MT-descriptive_analysis-how4.speaker: lockie
MT-descriptive_analysis-how4.text: The 2024 application planned correlation and regression (Appendix C.1); 'neither is run' (3.6).

MT-descriptive_analysis-how5.speaker: lockie
MT-descriptive_analysis-how5.text: Example cross-tabulation: collaborating now by size, 14 of 30 large (47 per cent), 13 of 34 medium (38), 9 of 45 small (20); rating trust at 5, 28 of 50 small (56), 19 of 35 medium (54), 21 of 34 large (62) (5.3).

MT-descriptive_analysis-why.speaker: lockie
MT-descriptive_analysis-why.text: Correlation and regression were not run 'because a sample that selected itself supports no estimate beyond itself (Fowler, 2014), and because the survey is used here to give scale to what the interviews heard of trust, not to measure the industry' (3.6).

MT-descriptive_analysis-not.speaker: lockie
MT-descriptive_analysis-not.text: Correlation and regression, as planned in 2024 (3.6; 3.8).

MT-descriptive_analysis-analogy.speaker: lockie
MT-descriptive_analysis-analogy.text: A census of one room: you can say exactly what this room thinks, not what the country thinks.

MV-descriptive_analysis-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-descriptive_analysis-v1.text: Why no significance tests on the survey?

MV-descriptive_analysis-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-descriptive_analysis-v2.text: What is a cross-tabulation, and how did you use it?

MQ-descriptive_analysis-q1.speaker: lockie
MQ-descriptive_analysis-q1.text: Why were correlation and regression not run on the survey?

MQ-descriptive_analysis-q2.speaker: lockie
MQ-descriptive_analysis-q2.text: Among large companies, what share collaborate now?

MT-directed_content_analysis-plain.speaker: sam
MT-directed_content_analysis-plain.text: Coding text against categories fixed in advance from a theory, with a written rule for each value, rather than letting categories emerge from the reading.

MT-directed_content_analysis-how1.speaker: sam
MT-directed_content_analysis-how1.text: 'The 117 arrangements were coded again in October 2026, for the fifth link, by directed content analysis (Hsieh and Shannon, 2005)' (3.4).

MT-directed_content_analysis-how2.speaker: sam
MT-directed_content_analysis-how2.text: 'A written codebook fixed the values and the decision rule for each variable, and each code was taken from the row of Appendix H and its passage in the transcript, with the quotation recorded' (3.4).

MT-directed_content_analysis-how3.speaker: sam
MT-directed_content_analysis-how3.text: The codebook ran in versions 1 to 3, piloted and coded twice (see codebook versions) (3.4; Appendix L).

MT-directed_content_analysis-how4.speaker: sam
MT-directed_content_analysis-how4.text: The aim in 4.4: 'so that what binds an arrangement could be set against the refusal of 4.2 on the same rows' (4.4).

MT-directed_content_analysis-why.speaker: sam
MT-directed_content_analysis-why.text: The thesis says what the coding was for (the fifth link, and setting what binds against the refusal on the same rows, 4.4) but does not say why the directed form was chosen over other forms of content analysis.

MT-directed_content_analysis-not.speaker: sam
MT-directed_content_analysis-not.text: The thematic and codebook codings of the transcripts, which are a different exercise on a different unit (3.4).

MT-directed_content_analysis-analogy.speaker: sam
MT-directed_content_analysis-analogy.text: Filling in a standard inspection form for every building on a street: the boxes are fixed in advance, and each tick must point to what the inspector saw.

MV-directed_content_analysis-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-directed_content_analysis-v1.text: Why directed content analysis for the arrangements?

MV-directed_content_analysis-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-directed_content_analysis-v2.text: What did each code rest on?

MQ-directed_content_analysis-q1.speaker: sam
MQ-directed_content_analysis-q1.text: Whose account of directed content analysis does 3.4 cite?

MQ-directed_content_analysis-q2.speaker: sam
MQ-directed_content_analysis-q2.text: When were the 117 arrangements coded by directed content analysis?

MG-directed_content_analysis.speaker: sam
MG-directed_content_analysis.text: Why directed content analysis rather than another form is not stated.

MT-document_analysis-plain.speaker: lockie
MT-document_analysis-plain.text: Reading an organisation's own documents systematically, for what they say, what they expected and what they leave out, as evidence in their own right.

MT-document_analysis-how1.speaker: lockie
MT-document_analysis-how1.text: Ghent was chosen as 'the one European city brought to the author's notice whose access regime writes hours into the permit itself, category by category and in law' (3.5).

MT-document_analysis-how2.speaker: lockie
MT-document_analysis-how2.text: 'The test was documentary, in the sense Bowen (2009) gives the term: a reading of the city's own record for what it says, what it expected and what it did not count' (3.5).

MT-document_analysis-how3.speaker: lockie
MT-document_analysis-how3.text: Two documents, both in Dutch: the draft circulation plan, Ontwerp Circulatieplan Binnenstad Gent, of 24 October 2016, 158 pages (chapter 7: 7.8 time windows, 7.10 permit categories, 7.11 the city's modelled expectation); and the Plan stedelijke logistiek of autumn 2023, 36 pages (3.5).

MT-document_analysis-how4.speaker: lockie
MT-document_analysis-how4.text: Eight questions were put to them: what the regime allocates (hours or space); to whom, by category; on what conditions; what 2023 withdrew or added; what the city expected the windows to do to delivery traffic; what frictions it recorded; whether either treats operators as competitors or mentions carriers sharing; and whether 2023 mentions neighbouring cities' windows (3.5). The answers are in 5.2.

MT-document_analysis-how5.speaker: lockie
MT-document_analysis-how5.text: 'The reading is a document analysis, not a case study in Yin's sense (2018), which would have needed the operators and the register as well as the plans' (3.5).

MT-document_analysis-how6.speaker: lockie
MT-document_analysis-how6.text: Belgian participants' accounts of window regimes are used with the other interviews in 5.1, not in the document reading (3.5).

MT-document_analysis-how7.speaker: lockie
MT-document_analysis-how7.text: The receiver's opening hours were not observed directly; they are read in participants' accounts and in the city's actor table, whose retailers' row gives 'deliveries within opening hours' as their interest (Stad Gent, 2023, p. 7) (3.5).

MT-document_analysis-why.speaker: lockie
MT-document_analysis-why.text: 'The documents are taken as the regime's own statement of itself, which is exactly what a test of a design proposition needs' (3.5).

MT-document_analysis-not.speaker: lockie
MT-document_analysis-not.text: A case study in Yin's sense, which would have needed the operators and the permit register (3.5).

MT-document_analysis-analogy.speaker: lockie
MT-document_analysis-analogy.text: Judging a company's plan by its own board papers: they tell you what it intended and expected, not what happened on the shop floor.

MV-document_analysis-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-document_analysis-v1.text: Why Ghent, and why only Ghent?

MV-document_analysis-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-document_analysis-v2.text: Why isn't this a case study?

MV-document_analysis-v3.speaker: dr_tally
MV-document_analysis-v3.text: What did the documents not count?

MQ-document_analysis-q1.text: Whose sense of documentary analysis does 3.5 follow?

MQ-document_analysis-q2.speaker: lockie
MQ-document_analysis-q2.text: How many questions were put to the Ghent documents?

MQ-document_analysis-q3.speaker: lockie
MQ-document_analysis-q3.text: Which date is the draft circulation plan?

MT-emergent_framework-plain.speaker: ada
MT-emergent_framework-plain.text: A framework drawn from the data during the research, rather than fixed beforehand and imposed on it.

MT-emergent_framework-how1.speaker: ada
MT-emergent_framework-how1.text: The fieldwork was designed under four pillars from the field as it stood in 2021: trust, efficiency, innovation, sustainability; the 2024 guide was built on them (2.7).

MT-emergent_framework-how2.speaker: ada
MT-emergent_framework-how2.text: The data replaced them (Figure 2.5): trust survived chiefly as something supplied from outside the parties (95 of 117 accounts bound from outside, six by their own trust); efficiency moved firms but could not on its own make rivals collaborate; innovation was a facilitator; sustainability was demoted to a by-product (2.7).

MT-emergent_framework-how3.speaker: ada
MT-emergent_framework-how3.text: Five concepts emerged. 'The first four concepts came out of the data before any theory named them.' The fifth, the holder, was drawn from the interviews read again beside the author's notes of 2022 and 2023, the locker networks, the rules and Chen's (1996) two kinds of overlap, and 'is a link the thesis proposes, not one it found' (2.7).

MT-emergent_framework-how4.speaker: ada
MT-emergent_framework-how4.text: 'The framework is emergent in the sense the methodology literature allows (Trafford and Leshem, 2008, pp. 84-87; Miles and Huberman, 1994): it was not imposed on the fieldwork, it was drawn from it, and Chapter 3 says how' (2.7).

MT-emergent_framework-how5.speaker: ada
MT-emergent_framework-how5.text: The sequence that shows it emerged is the three codings (1.6; 3.4).

MT-emergent_framework-why.speaker: ada
MT-emergent_framework-why.text: 'A framework that came out of the data is a stronger claim to conceptualisation than one fixed before the data arrived, as long as the thesis shows how it came about' (1.6); 'a framework that emerged in that order can be shown to have emerged, and one that had been imposed could not' (1.6). Critical realism is why 'Chapter 2 presents the framework as coming out of the evidence rather than being laid over it' (3.1).

MT-emergent_framework-not.speaker: ada
MT-emergent_framework-not.text: An imposed framework, which is what the four pillars were for the 2024 guide (2.7).

MT-emergent_framework-analogy.speaker: ada
MT-emergent_framework-analogy.text: Paths across a park worn by people walking, rather than paved in advance: the map is drawn from where feet actually went.

MV-emergent_framework-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-emergent_framework-v1.text: Your framework is in Chapter 2, but you say it emerged from the data. Isn't that back to front?

MV-emergent_framework-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-emergent_framework-v2.text: Which link did not emerge in the same way?

MQ-emergent_framework-q2.speaker: ada
MQ-emergent_framework-q2.text: What became of trust in the emergent framework?

MT-ethics_and_consent-term.speaker: sam
MT-ethics_and_consent-term.text: Ethics approval and consent (including verbal consent)

MT-ethics_and_consent-plain.speaker: sam
MT-ethics_and_consent-plain.text: Formal permission from a university ethics committee before research with people, and each participant's informed agreement to take part and be recorded.

MT-ethics_and_consent-how1.speaker: sam
MT-ethics_and_consent-how1.text: The School of Architecture and the Built Environment's ethics committee, Faculty of Science and Engineering, approved the study as Category A on 22 February 2024, with the guide, the participant information sheet and the consent form, on condition that the final questions be approved by the supervisory team before data collection began, 'which was done' (3.3; Appendices B, C).

MT-ethics_and_consent-how2.speaker: sam
MT-ethics_and_consent-how2.text: Every participant received the information sheet and consent form; twenty-seven of the thirty returned the form signed; three (A5, the second participant in A9, and B8) consented verbally, on the recording, B8 at the close of the call; B8 had been sent the sheet, which said the interview would be recorded and that recording could be declined (3.3).

MT-ethics_and_consent-how3.speaker: sam
MT-ethics_and_consent-how3.text: The survey ran under the same approval; its first item asked respondents to confirm they had read the information sheet, and the six who answered No are excluded; it asked for no name and no organisation; the optional email answers were not read (3.6).

MT-ethics_and_consent-why.speaker: sam
MT-ethics_and_consent-why.text: 'Ethics was part of the design and not a clearance obtained for it' (3.3). Verbal consent follows the ESRC, which holds that 'in some contexts verbal consent may be ethically preferable to written consent' and that 'Where possible this should include audio-recorded consent' (Economic and Social Research Council, 2026) (3.3).

MT-ethics_and_consent-analogy.speaker: sam
MT-ethics_and_consent-analogy.text: A building permit and the householder's signed agreement: the first says the work may be done at all, the second that this person agreed to it.

MV-ethics_and_consent-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-ethics_and_consent-v1.text: Three participants didn't sign a consent form. Is that a problem?

MV-ethics_and_consent-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-ethics_and_consent-v2.text: What condition did the ethics approval carry?

MQ-ethics_and_consent-q1.speaker: sam
MQ-ethics_and_consent-q1.text: When was the study approved, and in which category?

MQ-ethics_and_consent-q2.speaker: sam
MQ-ethics_and_consent-q2.text: How many of the thirty participants returned the consent form signed?

MT-finding_vs_proposition-plain.speaker: vera
MT-finding_vs_proposition-plain.text: A finding is something the evidence shows. A proposition is a claim the evidence points to and partly supports, offered for testing.

MT-finding_vs_proposition-how1.speaker: vera
MT-finding_vs_proposition-how1.text: Four links are found; the fifth is proposed: 'Link 5, the holder, is different. The thesis proposes it rather than finding it (6.3)' (1.5); 'Four of the five were there to be read in the evidence; the fifth, the holder, is where that evidence points' (2.7).

MT-finding_vs_proposition-how2.speaker: vera
MT-finding_vs_proposition-how2.text: The holder's evidence is graded: the interviews support it 'only under' rule 1a; the locker difference 'fits the link but does not test it'; and no rule found looks again when control changes (1.5).

MT-finding_vs_proposition-how3.speaker: vera
MT-finding_vs_proposition-how3.text: Ghent's 2016 expectation that suppliers' traffic would not fall in the open window was not counted in either plan, so 'Chapter 6 treats it as expected and not as found' (5.2).

MT-finding_vs_proposition-how4.speaker: vera
MT-finding_vs_proposition-how4.text: The one sentence is tested clause by clause and 'stands as a finding up to ‘the street’ and as a proposition after it' (6.5, Figure 6.7).

MT-finding_vs_proposition-how5.speaker: vera
MT-finding_vs_proposition-how5.text: Because the design is theory-building, even the found links are offered as propositions P1 to P5 for others to test (7.2).

MT-finding_vs_proposition-why.speaker: vera
MT-finding_vs_proposition-why.text: For the holder, three reasons the thesis gives: the interviews support it only under a rule added after the results were seen; the locker test shows a difference by owner class, 'consistent with the clause and not a test of it'; and 'no city has yet done what the clause says' (6.5).

MT-finding_vs_proposition-analogy.speaker: vera
MT-finding_vs_proposition-analogy.text: A weather service reports yesterday's rainfall as a finding; tomorrow's forecast, however well grounded, is a proposition until tomorrow comes.

MV-finding_vs_proposition-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-finding_vs_proposition-v1.text: Which parts of your one sentence are findings, and which are propositions?

MV-finding_vs_proposition-v1-ans.speaker: marigold
MV-finding_vs_proposition-v1-ans.text: Up to 'the street' it is a finding: competition for the same customers, not a shortage of trust, stops carriers collaborating, and where they cannot share the street the line falls at the customer relationship. After it, that what they would share must be held by someone who does not want their customers and that a city can see it stays that way, it is a proposition: no city has yet done what the last clause says (6.5).

MV-finding_vs_proposition-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-finding_vs_proposition-v2.text: You have p = .008 on the lockers. Why not claim the holder as a finding?

MV-finding_vs_proposition-v2-ans.speaker: marigold
MV-finding_vs_proposition-v2-ans.text: Because that is a difference by owner class at one time, consistent with the link and not a test of it; the interviews support the holder only under a coding rule added after the results were seen; and no rule found looks again when control changes. So I propose it, with its objections and its tests (1.5; 5.2; 6.5; 7.4).

MQ-finding_vs_proposition-q1.speaker: vera
MQ-finding_vs_proposition-q1.text: Which link does the thesis propose rather than find?

MQ-finding_vs_proposition-q2.speaker: vera
MQ-finding_vs_proposition-q2.text: How does the thesis treat Ghent's 2016 expectation that suppliers' traffic would not fall in the open window?

MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-term.speaker: lockie
MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-term.text: Fisher's exact test, and why non-independent pairs make it indicative

MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-plain.speaker: lockie
MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-plain.text: Fisher's exact test checks whether two yes/no categories are related in a small table of counts. It assumes each counted item is independent; if items are linked, its p value overstates the certainty.

MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-how1.speaker: lockie
MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-how1.text: The test compares carriers' delivery into neutral-held and rival-held networks 'by Fisher's exact test on the carriers' (3.5).

MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-how2.speaker: lockie
MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-how2.text: Pairs with evidence: the carrier delivers in 45 of 48 neutral-held pairs and 18 of 44 rival-held (5.2).

MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-how3.speaker: lockie
MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-how3.text: Pairs with each country's main carriers: 41 of 88 and 18 of 86 (5.2).

MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-how4.speaker: lockie
MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-how4.text: Fisher's exact test, p < .001 for both (two-sided, Appendix M) (5.2).

MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-how5.speaker: lockie
MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-how5.text: 'The pairs are not independent, because one network serves several carriers and one carrier faces several networks, so these two p-values are indicative, and the permutation test above, which counts each ownership period once, is the result the thesis rests on' (5.2).

MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-why.speaker: lockie
MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-why.text: The thesis reports both tests and rests on the permutation test because the pairs are not independent (5.2). It does not say why Fisher's exact test in particular was chosen for the pairs.

MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-not.speaker: lockie
MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-not.text: Relying on the pair-level p values (rejected as only indicative, 5.2).

MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-analogy.speaker: lockie
MT-fishers_exact_and_dependence-analogy.text: Polling ten members of one family counts as ten votes, but they are not ten independent opinions.

MV-fishers_exact_and_dependence-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-fishers_exact_and_dependence-v1.text: Your Fisher's test gives p < .001. Why not lead with it?

MV-fishers_exact_and_dependence-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-fishers_exact_and_dependence-v2.text: Do the pair counts and the period counts agree?

MQ-fishers_exact_and_dependence-q1.speaker: lockie
MQ-fishers_exact_and_dependence-q1.text: Why are the Fisher p values only indicative?

MQ-fishers_exact_and_dependence-q2.speaker: lockie
MQ-fishers_exact_and_dependence-q2.text: In how many of the 48 neutral-held pairs with evidence does the carrier deliver?

MG-fishers_exact_and_dependence.speaker: lockie
MG-fishers_exact_and_dependence.text: Why Fisher's exact test was chosen for the pairs is not stated.

MT-framework_tests-term.speaker: ada
MT-framework_tests-term.text: Testing a framework: Berger and Patchner's three questions and the critical test

MT-framework_tests-plain.speaker: ada
MT-framework_tests-plain.text: Checks a conceptual framework should pass: is its theory described and tied to the problem, does a theory sit under the question, and do its parts hang together and direct the research.

MT-framework_tests-how1.speaker: ada
MT-framework_tests-how1.text: Berger and Patchner (1988, cited in Trafford and Leshem, 2008, p. 85) ask three questions, each answered in 2.7: is the theoretical base clearly described and related to the problem (2.6; 2.4); is there a theory underlying the research question (both halves answered: overlap and binding as conditions; a rule on who holds the shared point beside an access rule by vehicle and hour); is the connection between theory, earlier findings and purpose explicit (Table 2.2; each link serves the objective with its number).

MT-framework_tests-how2.speaker: ada
MT-framework_tests-how2.text: Trafford and Leshem's 'critical' test (2008, p. 87): unity (Table 2.2, 'no theory is asked to do another's job'); direction (Chapter 3: the unit of analysis, the two codebooks, the two units of counting and the two further units follow from the links); meaning (Chapter 6, each finding read back through its link); coherence (Chapter 7's conceptual conclusions) (2.7).

MT-framework_tests-how3.speaker: ada
MT-framework_tests-how3.text: Each concept is a variable with a definition, values and a disconfirming observation: overlap takes yes, no, partly, unclear; binding takes one of ten values; the holder one of six classes (2.7).

MT-framework_tests-why.speaker: ada
MT-framework_tests-why.text: Offered as the tests a framework should meet in the methodology literature the thesis follows (2.7). No further reason is given.

MT-framework_tests-analogy.speaker: ada
MT-framework_tests-analogy.text: A bridge load test before opening: anchored at both ends, carries the weight it was built for, and its parts act as one structure.

MV-framework_tests-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-framework_tests-v1.text: How do you know your framework is a framework and not a list?

MV-framework_tests-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-framework_tests-v2.text: What would count against your overlap concept?

MQ-framework_tests-q1.speaker: ada
MQ-framework_tests-q1.text: Which of these is NOT part of the critical test as 2.7 applies it?

MQ-framework_tests-q2.speaker: ada
MQ-framework_tests-q2.text: How many values can 'binding' take in 2.7?

MT-fulltext_rerun-plain.speaker: ada
MT-fulltext_rerun-plain.text: Going back to a past screening stage and making a fresh, recorded decision on each paper that could have been excluded there, because the original record gave only general reasons.

MT-fulltext_rerun-how1.speaker: ada
MT-fulltext_rerun-how1.text: The 2023 record gives its exclusion reasons at the full-text stage by topic, among them 'crowd-shipping, travelling salesman problems, bicycle deliveries, and public transport sharing', not paper by paper (2.1).

MT-fulltext_rerun-how2.speaker: ada
MT-fulltext_rerun-how2.text: In 2026, 'the thirty-one papers that could have left at that stage were each assessed again against the 2023 criteria and coded twice, with every disagreement settled' (3.2).

MT-fulltext_rerun-how3.speaker: ada
MT-fulltext_rerun-how3.text: Twenty-nine exclusions were upheld; two papers meet the criteria, and the forty-nine already include studies of the same kinds, 'so leaving those two out does not change the kinds of study the review covers' (3.2).

MT-fulltext_rerun-how4.speaker: ada
MT-fulltext_rerun-how4.text: On subject the two codings agreed on thirty of thirty-one (alpha = .91); six further codes differed on publication type alone, all papers in conference proceedings, a kind the forty-nine include, and were settled by that precedent (3.2).

MT-fulltext_rerun-how5.speaker: ada
MT-fulltext_rerun-how5.text: Appendix E gives each candidate with its settled code and reason, dated to the re-run (3.2). Recorded as change 4 in Table 3.8.

MT-fulltext_rerun-how6.speaker: ada
MT-fulltext_rerun-how6.text: Why thirty-one: no list of the seventy-two survives; the candidates are the thirty records in the 2023 full-text export that are not among the forty-nine, plus Kanter (1994), the one hand-added paper not among them (Appendix E, E.2.7 and E.2.10).

MT-fulltext_rerun-why.speaker: ada
MT-fulltext_rerun-why.text: It answers PRISMA 2020 item 16b, which asks a review 'to cite the studies that might appear to meet its criteria and to say why each was excluded' (Page et al., 2021) (3.2); and 'the 2023 record gave its exclusion reasons by topic and did not name the papers it excluded at that stage' (Table 3.8).

MT-fulltext_rerun-analogy.speaker: ada
MT-fulltext_rerun-analogy.text: Re-marking a batch of exam scripts where the original marker left only a general comment, so each script now carries its own mark and reason.

MV-fulltext_rerun-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-fulltext_rerun-v1.text: Seventy-two read in full and forty-nine included is twenty-three dropped. Why did you reassess thirty-one?

MQ-fulltext_rerun-q1.speaker: ada
MQ-fulltext_rerun-q1.text: Why was the 2023 full-text stage re-run?

MQ-fulltext_rerun-q2.speaker: ada
MQ-fulltext_rerun-q2.text: How many exclusions did the re-run uphold?

MQ-fulltext_rerun-q3.speaker: ada
MQ-fulltext_rerun-q3.text: What agreement did the two codings of the re-run reach on subject?

MG-fulltext_rerun.speaker: ada
MG-fulltext_rerun.text: The main text does not reconcile thirty-one candidates with the twenty-three papers dropped between seventy-two and forty-nine; only Appendix E does. Know the appendix answer.

MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-term.speaker: nora
MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-term.text: Generalising to the mechanism, not the population (analytical generalisation)

MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-plain.speaker: nora
MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-plain.text: Instead of claiming a result holds for a whole population, the claim is that a mechanism has been identified that may operate elsewhere, under the right conditions. Methodologists often call this analytical generalisation.

MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-how1.speaker: nora
MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-how1.text: Table 3.2, critical realist column: findings generalise 'To the mechanism, not the population; it may fire elsewhere under other conditions (Easton, 2010)'.

MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-how2.speaker: nora
MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-how2.text: 'A mechanism named from twenty-six accounts is a proposition, and what it generalises to is the mechanism, which may work elsewhere, not a population' (3.1).

MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-how3.speaker: nora
MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-how3.text: Propositions are 'claimed for the mechanism it names, not for a population (7.4)' (7.2).

MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-how4.speaker: nora
MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-how4.text: 7.4: the propositions 'rest on the cases from which they were drawn, are offered as propositions about mechanisms rather than as generalisations about populations, and are open to others to test'.

MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-how5.speaker: nora
MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-how5.text: Transferability is met by thick description, by code and type, for a reader to judge where the findings travel (3.7).

MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-how6.speaker: nora
MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-how6.text: The thesis does not use the phrase 'analytical generalisation'; it says 'generalises to the mechanism'.

MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-why.speaker: nora
MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-why.text: It is the generalisation critical realism allows (Table 3.2; 7.4): 'The generalisation the paradigm allows is the one the propositions of 7.2 claim' (7.4).

MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-not.speaker: nora
MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-not.text: Statistical generalisation from sample to population (positivist), and no generalisation, transferability left to the reader (interpretivist) (Table 3.2).

MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-analogy.speaker: nora
MT-generalisation_to_mechanism-analogy.text: Learning how a lock's mechanism works from a handful of locks: it tells you how any lock of that design can be opened, not how many such locks exist.

MV-generalisation_to_mechanism-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-generalisation_to_mechanism-v1.text: Is this what's called analytical generalisation?

MV-generalisation_to_mechanism-v1-ans.speaker: marigold
MV-generalisation_to_mechanism-v1-ans.text: That's the usual label for what I claim, though the thesis puts it in its own words: a mechanism named from twenty-six accounts generalises to the mechanism, not to a population; it may fire elsewhere under other conditions. The propositions rest on the cases they were drawn from and are open to others to test (3.1; Table 3.2; 7.4).

MV-generalisation_to_mechanism-v2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
MV-generalisation_to_mechanism-v2.text: How is that different from transferability?

MV-generalisation_to_mechanism-v2-ans.speaker: marigold
MV-generalisation_to_mechanism-v2-ans.text: Transferability is the reader's judgement on a thick description, and I support it with description by code and type across eleven countries. My claim goes a step further than an interpretivist would, that a mechanism may fire elsewhere under other conditions, and still stops short of a population (3.7; Table 3.2).

MQ-generalisation_to_mechanism-q1.speaker: nora
MQ-generalisation_to_mechanism-q1.text: According to Table 3.2, how do critical realist findings generalise?

MG-generalisation_to_mechanism.speaker: nora
MG-generalisation_to_mechanism.text: The thesis never uses the term 'analytical generalisation'. If an examiner uses it, accept the label and give the thesis's own wording.

MT-information_power-term.speaker: sam
MT-information_power-term.text: Information power (how many interviews are enough)

MT-information_power-plain.speaker: sam
MT-information_power-plain.text: The idea that a study needs fewer interviews the more information each one holds for its aim: a narrow aim, well-chosen participants, guiding theory and strong conversations all reduce the number needed.

MT-information_power-how1.speaker: sam
MT-information_power-how1.text: Malterud, Siersma and Guassora (2016) 'hold that the number of interviews a study needs falls as its aim narrows, as the sample's specificity to that aim rises, as the study is guided by theory, as the dialogue is strong and as the analysis is of cases rather than across them' (3.3).

MT-information_power-how2.speaker: sam
MT-information_power-how2.text: On the first four, this study's need was low: its aim was narrow; its participants were chosen for having convened, funded, regulated, brokered or refused the very thing at issue; its coding was against a stated framework; and sixteen of the twenty-six interviews ran forty minutes or more (3.3).

MT-information_power-how3.speaker: sam
MT-information_power-how3.text: On the fifth it was higher, 'since the analysis runs across cases' (3.3).

MT-information_power-why.speaker: sam
MT-information_power-why.text: Given as the argument for why twenty-six was enough, beside saturation (3.3).

MT-information_power-not.speaker: sam
MT-information_power-not.text: Guest, Bunce and Johnson's (2006) dozen-interview finding, not relied on (see saturation). The phrase 'information power' appears only in the title of Malterud and colleagues' paper; the body of 3.3 uses their five dimensions without naming the concept.

MT-information_power-analogy.speaker: sam
MT-information_power-analogy.text: How many witnesses you need depends on who they are: five people who stood at the junction tell you more than fifty who heard about it later.

MV-information_power-v1.speaker: dr_tally
MV-information_power-v1.text: How did you decide twenty-six interviews was enough?

MQ-information_power-q1.speaker: sam
MQ-information_power-q1.text: On which of Malterud and colleagues' dimensions was this study's need higher?

MQ-information_power-q2.speaker: sam
MQ-information_power-q2.text: How many of the twenty-six interviews ran forty minutes or more?

MG-information_power.speaker: sam
MG-information_power.text: The thesis argues Malterud's dimensions but never uses the term 'information power' in its text. Use the term if asked, then give the five dimensions.

MT-interviewer_effects-term.speaker: sam
MT-interviewer_effects-term.text: Interviewer effects: seeded themes, relayed positions and the five cautions

MT-interviewer_effects-plain.speaker: sam
MT-interviewer_effects-plain.text: An interviewer can shape answers by suggesting ideas or repeating what others said. Good practice records where that happened and does not count it as the participant's own view.

MT-interviewer_effects-how1.speaker: sam
MT-interviewer_effects-how1.text: Each coding recorded, transcript by transcript, the themes the interviewer introduced and the positions he relayed between interviews, 'and neither is counted as a participant's view' (4.1).

MT-interviewer_effects-how2.speaker: sam
MT-interviewer_effects-how2.text: Brand, raised by the interviewer in five interviews, was declined in all five, and is counted as declined, not as absent; it was raised unprompted in eight, three of them first-hand (3.4; 4.6).

MT-interviewer_effects-how3.speaker: sam
