QZ-app-C-q2.text: In which category was the study approved?

QZ-app-C-q3.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-C-q3.text: What condition came with the approval?

QZ-app-C-q4.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-C-q4.text: What analysis did the application plan for the survey?

QZ-app-C-q5.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-C-q5.text: What date does the draft survey carry?

QZ-app-C-q6.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-C-q6.text: What was the longest duration option in the draft survey?

QZ-app-C-q7.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-C-q7.text: What was the project title on the ethics application?

EL-ethics_office-HELLO.speaker: clement
EL-ethics_office-HELLO.text: Clement Stamp, ethics officer. Welcome to the Ethics Office. Everything in here gets stamped twice.

CN-R-J.speaker: marigold
CN-R-J.text: Ghent Gate: the city's Dutch extracts, each beside its English rendering.

EL-ghent_gate_room-L01.speaker: lotte
EL-ghent_gate_room-L01.text: Overlapping permit categories cut back, almost all open around the clock.

EL-ghent_gate_room-L02.speaker: lotte
EL-ghent_gate_room-L02.text: Loading and unloading: the one windowed category.

EL-ghent_gate_room-L03.speaker: lotte
EL-ghent_gate_room-L03.text: Cameras and a fine. The permit itself costs nothing.

EL-ghent_gate_room-L04.speaker: lotte
EL-ghent_gate_room-L04.text: The sentence that matters, in Dutch first.

EL-ghent_gate_room-L05.speaker: lotte
EL-ghent_gate_room-L05.text: Mind the word venstertijd: same hours, flipped label.

EL-ghent_gate_room-TR-N.speaker: marigold
EL-ghent_gate_room-TR-N.text: Digits nods at the city hall.

EL-ghent_gate_room-TR-D.speaker: digits
EL-ghent_gate_room-TR-D.text: Who starts these things? Where's that counted?

EL-ghent_gate_room-GR.speaker: grill
EL-ghent_gate_room-GR.text: So this is a case study of Ghent, is it?

EL-ghent_gate_room-GIST.speaker: marigold
EL-ghent_gate_room-GIST.text: No, a document analysis: the plans read as the regime's statement of what it allocates and expected, not its street practice.

EL-ghent_gate_room-WFB1.speaker: grill
EL-ghent_gate_room-WFB1.text: Misnames it. Without the operators and the permit register it is a document analysis.

EL-ghent_gate_room-WFB2.speaker: grill
EL-ghent_gate_room-WFB2.text: Claims cause. The documents say what the regime allocates and expected, not what it achieves.

EL-ghent_gate_room-MG1.speaker: grill
EL-ghent_gate_room-MG1.text: You don't speak Dutch. Why should I trust your renderings?

EL-CARD-app-J-what.speaker: marigold
EL-CARD-app-J-what.text: The Dutch passages from Ghent's two city plans that the thesis relies on, each set beside Khaled's English rendering, with answers to eight questions about how Ghent's delivery permits and hours work.

EL-CARD-app-J-why.speaker: marigold
EL-CARD-app-J-why.text: Backs 3.5 (the document analysis, Scott's four tests, and how the renderings were checked), 5.2 (Ghent's regime and the rule by vehicle and hour; Figures 5.1 and 5.2), 3.8 change 5 (the city expected no fall in suppliers' traffic in the open hours) and 7.4 (the limit that no Dutch speaker checked the renderings).

AF-J-f2.speaker: marigold
AF-J-f2.text: Document 1 is the draft circulation plan of 24 October 2016, 158 PDF pages, for introduction on 3 April 2017; chapter 7 sets the access regime.

AF-J-f3.speaker: marigold
AF-J-f3.text: Document 2 is the urban logistics plan of autumn 2023, 36 pages: a policy plan, not a regulation.

AF-J-f4.speaker: marigold
AF-J-f4.text: The 2016 plan replaced 26 overlapping permit categories with fourteen; thirteen get 24/24 access and only loading and unloading is windowed.

AF-J-f5.speaker: marigold
AF-J-f5.text: Loading and unloading is allowed 18:00 to 11:00 in the four central areas (05:00 to 19:00 in the Overpoortstraat area); the closed period is 11:00 to 18:00.

AF-J-f6.speaker: marigold
AF-J-f6.text: Enforcement is by 27 ANPR cameras and a €55 administrative fine; the permit is free.

AF-J-f7.speaker: marigold
AF-J-f7.text: The city's own model expected delivery traffic in the open window to stay the same size.

AF-J-f8.speaker: marigold
AF-J-f8.text: For 11:00 to 18:00 the city expected at most a third of traffic to remain in streets without public transport, and half in streets with it.

AF-J-f9.speaker: marigold
AF-J-f9.text: After the 2016 dialogue the closed period for deliveries was cut from 11:00-19:00 to 11:00-18:00.

AF-J-f10.speaker: marigold
AF-J-f10.text: The word 'venstertijd' means the open delivery window in 2016 but the closed period in 2023; the hours are the same and only the label flips.

AF-J-f11.speaker: marigold
AF-J-f11.text: In the 2016 plan the printed page number is one lower than the PDF page, because the cover is page 0; the thesis cites printed pages.

AF-J-f12.speaker: marigold
AF-J-f12.text: Neither document describes delivery operators as competitors of one another.

EQ-app-J-eq1.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-app-J-eq1.text: You don't speak Dutch. How can we trust your renderings?

MA-app-J-eq1.speaker: marigold
MA-app-J-eq1.text: Each rendering was made for this thesis and checked against the Dutch original, against a second translation made independently of the first, and against a dictionary. No Dutch speaker checked them, and I carry that as a limit in 7.4. That's exactly why every extract sits in Dutch beside the English in Appendix J: the reader, not me, has the last word on each.

MA-app-J-eq2.speaker: marigold
MA-app-J-eq2.text: It's the one European city brought to my notice whose access regime writes hours into the permit itself, category by category and in law. So it was the natural test of the fifth link as it was then framed: time allocated by a city (3.5, 5.2).

EQ-app-J-eq3.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-app-J-eq3.text: What did the Ghent documents show you?

MA-app-J-eq3.speaker: marigold
MA-app-J-eq3.text: That the city's own model expected delivery traffic in the open window to stay the same size (2016 plan, p. 112). The windows take deliveries out of the closed hours; they don't make suppliers share. That, with Ostrom's point that a rule which must know who is acting costs more to watch, is why I re-specified the fifth link from hours allocated to operators to the holder of the shared point, keeping the rule by vehicle and hour as the penalty (3.8, change 5).

EQ-app-J-eq4.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-app-J-eq4.text: Is this a case study of Ghent?

MA-app-J-eq4.speaker: marigold
MA-app-J-eq4.text: No, a document analysis. A case study in Yin's sense would have needed the operators and the permit register as well as the plans. I read the documents as the regime's own statement of what it allocates and expected, which is what a test of a design proposition needs; what the regime does on the street is the next study's question (3.5, 3.7).

EQ-app-J-eq5.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-app-J-eq5.text: Did Ghent measure the effect afterwards?

MA-app-J-eq5.speaker: marigold
MA-app-J-eq5.text: Not in these documents. The 2016 plan promised an evaluation of the categories after one year and a counts report in early 2018, and the 2023 plan reports none of those results (J (e)).

QZ-app-J-q1.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-J-q1.text: How many extracts does Appendix J give?

QZ-app-J-q2.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-J-q2.text: What is the date of Ghent's draft circulation plan?

QZ-app-J-q3.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-J-q3.text: How many permit categories did the 2016 plan create?

QZ-app-J-q4.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-J-q4.text: What is the closed period for deliveries in Ghent's car-free areas?

QZ-app-J-q5.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-J-q5.text: What did Ghent's own model expect for suppliers' traffic in the open window?

QZ-app-J-q6.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-J-q6.text: How is Ghent's access regime enforced, according to the 2016 plan?

QZ-app-J-q7.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-J-q7.text: What does 'venstertijd' name in each plan?

EL-ghent_gate_room-HELLO.speaker: lotte
EL-ghent_gate_room-HELLO.text: Lotte Brug. Welcome to Ghent Gate. Dutch on the left, English on the right.

CN-R-A-G.speaker: marigold
CN-R-A-G.text: The Interview Café: the questions you took into every interview, and the table of who took part.

EL-interview_cafe-L01.speaker: vera
EL-interview_cafe-L01.text: I keep a copy of the pocket card you carried: the guide the committee approved.

EL-interview_cafe-L02.speaker: vera
EL-interview_cafe-L02.text: Most of its headings are your pillars. Recognise them?

EL-interview_cafe-L03.speaker: vera
EL-interview_cafe-L03.text: And your script asked straight out about trust, because the field did.

EL-interview_cafe-L04.speaker: vera
EL-interview_cafe-L04.text: The guest register: codes and roles, never names, and how long everyone stayed.

EL-interview_cafe-L05.speaker: vera
EL-interview_cafe-L05.text: Countries only as a set. A country beside a code could name someone.

EL-interview_cafe-TR-N.speaker: marigold
EL-interview_cafe-TR-N.text: Digits slides a napkin across the counter.

EL-interview_cafe-TR-D.speaker: digits
EL-interview_cafe-TR-D.text: This lot. Where's the table that holds it?

EL-interview_cafe-GR.speaker: grill
EL-interview_cafe-GR.text: Hardly any carrier voices, and some transcripts off the subject. Is this about carriers, or about people who talk about them?

EL-interview_cafe-GIST.speaker: marigold
EL-interview_cafe-GIST.text: Carriers are the one kind I call thin. The rest dealt with them for years, and no finding rests on the off-topic transcripts.

EL-interview_cafe-WFB1.speaker: grill
EL-interview_cafe-WFB1.text: Overclaims. Say thin first, then why the rest still counts.

EL-interview_cafe-WFB2.speaker: grill
EL-interview_cafe-WFB2.text: Over-concedes. Thin is not wrong: no finding rests on the off-topic transcripts alone.

EL-interview_cafe-MG1.speaker: grill
EL-interview_cafe-MG1.text: Some of your transcripts are thin or incomplete. Which ones, and what did you do?

EL-CARD-app-A-what.speaker: marigold
EL-CARD-app-A-what.text: The questions Khaled took into every interview: the short guide the ethics committee approved, and the longer working script he kept beside it.

EL-CARD-app-A-why.speaker: marigold
EL-CARD-app-A-why.text: Backs 3.3, which says the instrument approved on 22 February 2024 asked fourteen questions under seven headings and that a twenty-three-prompt script in ten stages sat beside it; and 2.7, which says the guide was built on the four pillars (trust, efficiency, innovation, sustainability) and produced the twenty-six conversations of Chapter 4.

EL-CARD-app-G-what.speaker: marigold
EL-CARD-app-G-what.text: A table of all 26 interviews: who took part (by type and code only), how long each lasted, how it was recorded and how consent was given.

EL-CARD-app-G-why.speaker: marigold
EL-CARD-app-G-why.text: Backs 3.3, whose Table 3.4 is the short form and points to Appendix G for the full table: twenty-six interviews, thirty people, eleven countries, twenty hours and five minutes, 146,778 words.

AF-A-f1.speaker: marigold
AF-A-f1.text: The approved guide asks fourteen questions under seven headings, two to each heading.

AF-A-f2.speaker: marigold
AF-A-f2.text: Four of the seven headings are the pillars of the registration.

AF-A-f3.speaker: marigold
AF-A-f3.text: The other three headings frame the conversation.

AF-A-f4.speaker: marigold
AF-A-f4.text: The working script has twenty-three numbered questions in ten stages, from Introduction to Closing.

AF-A-f5.speaker: marigold
AF-A-f5.text: Stage 9 of the script asks for further contacts (Questions 22 and 23), which is the chain referral described in 3.3.

AF-A-f6.speaker: marigold
AF-A-f6.text: The introduction script tells the participant the interview will last about 45 to 60 minutes.

AF-A-f7.speaker: marigold
AF-A-f7.text: The introduction script frames the research around competitive advantage through the four pillars.

AF-A-f8.speaker: marigold
AF-A-f8.text: The script defines horizontal collaboration as businesses at the same level of the supply chain working together.

AF-A-f9.speaker: marigold
AF-A-f9.text: Question 14 of the script asks directly about trust, which is why the thesis says the guide asked about trust because the field did.

EQ-app-A-eq1.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-app-A-eq1.text: Your guide was built on four pillars that your findings overturned. Didn't the guide steer your participants?

MA-app-A-eq1.speaker: marigold
MA-app-A-eq1.text: The guide asked about trust because the field did; that's where I started, and I quote the headings word for word in 3.3 as evidence of it. But I didn't analyse the data under those headings. The later codings were made against the working claim and then the five-concept codebook, and each had to record the evidence against as well as for. Where I raised a theme myself, like brand, I counted it as declined, not as support: I raised brand in five interviews and it was declined in all five.

EQ-app-A-eq2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-app-A-eq2.text: Why did you use two instruments, a guide and a script?

MA-app-A-eq2.speaker: marigold
MA-app-A-eq2.text: The fourteen-question guide is the one the ethics committee approved. The twenty-three-prompt script sat beside it so the conversation could follow the participant rather than the headings. That's the semi-structured form Brinkmann and Kvale describe: the themes are fixed, and the order and follow-up are left to the conversation (3.3).

EQ-app-A-eq3.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-app-A-eq3.text: You planned 45 to 60 minutes, but many interviews were shorter. Does that weaken the data?

MA-app-A-eq3.speaker: marigold
MA-app-A-eq3.text: They ran from eight minutes to seventy-four, with a median of forty-three, and sixteen of the twenty-six ran forty minutes or more. Fourteen closed sooner than planned, most because the person had said what they came to say. The shortest, A5, is eight minutes of prepared answers, and the coding files flag it, so no finding rests on it.

EQ-app-A-eq4.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-app-A-eq4.text: How did you find your participants?

MA-app-A-eq4.speaker: marigold
MA-app-A-eq4.text: Purposively, for the kinds of party the question needed, through the projects and publications in which they'd done the work. Then by referral: the script's ninth stage asks who else I should hear. I started chains from each of the three kinds of party, in eleven countries, to limit the bias that referrals run along one person's network (3.3).

QZ-app-A-q1.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-A-q1.text: How many questions did the interview guide approved by the ethics committee ask?

QZ-app-A-q2.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-A-q2.text: How many stages did the working script have?

QZ-app-A-q3.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-A-q3.text: Which of these is NOT one of the four pillar headings in the guide?

QZ-app-A-q4.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-A-q4.text: How long did the introduction script tell participants the interview would last?

QZ-app-A-q5.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-A-q5.text: Which stage of the working script asks the participant to suggest further interviewees?

QZ-app-A-q6.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-A-q6.text: On what date was the interview guide approved?

AF-G-f2.speaker: marigold
AF-G-f2.text: Twenty hours and five minutes of recording; median 42:40; shortest 7:57 (A5); longest 1:13:45 (B1).

AF-G-f3.speaker: marigold
AF-G-f3.text: Twenty-four recorded with video and two as audio, A3 and B8.

AF-G-f4.speaker: marigold
AF-G-f4.text: Twenty-seven consents signed and three given verbally on the recording.

AF-G-f5.speaker: marigold
AF-G-f5.text: The transcripts hold 146,778 words of speech, appended summaries excluded.

AF-G-f6.speaker: marigold
AF-G-f6.text: Countries are given only as a set: Belgium, Estonia, France, Germany, Greece, India, Italy, Norway, Spain, Sweden and the United Kingdom; two interviews spoke Europe-wide.

AF-G-f7.speaker: marigold
AF-G-f7.text: Twenty-three interviews were with one person, two with a pair (A4, A9) and one with three people from one European project (B7).

AF-G-f8.speaker: marigold
AF-G-f8.text: Sixteen of the twenty-six ran forty minutes or more.

AF-G-f9.speaker: marigold
AF-G-f9.text: By party: eight public bodies, six academia, four consultancies, four carriers, and one each platform, coalition, city network and site host.

AF-G-f10.speaker: marigold
AF-G-f10.text: Each length is the recording's length, confirmed against the last timestamp in the transcript.

EQ-app-G-eq1.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-app-G-eq1.text: Only four carrier voices. Isn't your account of carriers second-hand?

MA-app-G-eq1.speaker: marigold
MA-app-G-eq1.text: Partly, and I say so in 3.7. Four of the twenty-six speak for a carrier, three from inside one and one as adviser to a cargo-bike operator. The rest are people who convene, fund, regulate, study or broker collaboration, and have negotiated with carriers for years. Saturation was reached by kind of party, not by count, which is why carriers are the one kind I call thin.

EQ-app-G-eq2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-app-G-eq2.text: Why don't you give a country against each code?

MA-app-G-eq2.speaker: marigold
MA-app-G-eq2.text: Because a country plus a role could identify someone. I give the eleven countries as a set, describe organisations by type, and widen any role that would narrow to one person (3.3; G.1).

EQ-app-G-eq3.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-app-G-eq3.text: A5 lasted under eight minutes. Why keep it?

MA-app-G-eq3.speaker: marigold
MA-app-G-eq3.text: Every transcript stands in every count of twenty-six, so dropping it would be a choice made after the fact. It's flagged as thin: eight minutes of prepared answers, and its 'successes' are conference proposals. No finding rests on it (4.1; Appendix I, file 1 cautions).

EQ-app-G-eq4.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-app-G-eq4.text: How do you know the lengths are accurate?

MA-app-G-eq4.speaker: marigold
MA-app-G-eq4.text: Each is the recording's length, confirmed against the last timestamp in its transcript (G.1).

QZ-app-G-q1.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-G-q1.text: How much recording do the twenty-six interviews add up to?

QZ-app-G-q2.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-G-q2.text: What is the median interview length?

QZ-app-G-q4.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-G-q4.text: How many words of speech do the transcripts hold?

QZ-app-G-q5.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-G-q5.text: How many interviews were recorded as audio only?

QZ-app-G-q6.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-G-q6.text: How many interviews involved more than one participant?

QZ-app-G-q7.speaker: marigold
QZ-app-G-q7.text: How many interviews ran forty minutes or more?

EL-interview_cafe-HELLO.speaker: vera
EL-interview_cafe-HELLO.text: Vera Static, Freight FM. Welcome to the Interview Café. Grab a stool, the mic's warm.

CN-R-M.speaker: marigold
CN-R-M.text: The Locker Market: the review of locker networks, and the rules that call a point neutral.

EL-locker_market_room-L01.speaker: lockie
EL-locker_market_room-L01.text: One row per ownership period, so a network that changes hands gets a new row.

EL-locker_market_room-L02.speaker: lockie
EL-locker_market_room-L02.text: The main test, each ownership period counted once.

EL-locker_market_room-L03.speaker: lockie
EL-locker_market_room-L03.text: Same carrier, different holders: direction, not proof.

EL-locker_market_room-L04.speaker: lockie
EL-locker_market_room-L04.text: A sale gives a baseline: the same partners still listed weeks later.

EL-locker_market_room-L05.speaker: lockie
EL-locker_market_room-L05.text: What it doesn't show: quality, price, terms.

EL-locker_market_room-L06.speaker: lockie
EL-locker_market_room-L06.text: The search log, beyond its rules, is held by the author, available on request.

EL-locker_market_room-TR-D.speaker: digits
EL-locker_market_room-TR-D.text: Neutral against rival. Where's the test?

EL-locker_market_room-GR.speaker: grill
EL-locker_market_room-GR.text: Unmatched networks and a handful of ownership periods. You call that a sample?

EL-locker_market_room-GIST.speaker: marigold
EL-locker_market_room-GIST.text: It shows a difference by owner class at one time, not the per-pair form; I rest on the permutation test and run no regression.

EL-locker_market_room-WFB1.speaker: grill
EL-locker_market_room-WFB1.text: Claims cause. A difference by owner class at one time is not proof.

EL-locker_market_room-WFB2.speaker: grill
EL-locker_market_room-WFB2.text: Over-concedes. It is consistent with the link, one of three kinds of evidence, and you say which.

EL-CARD-app-M-what.speaker: marigold
EL-CARD-app-M-what.text: A repeatable search of Europe's parcel-locker and pick-up-point networks and of the rules that call a shared point neutral, testing whether carriers deliver into networks held by a neutral firm more than into ones held by a rival.

EL-CARD-app-M-why.speaker: marigold
EL-CARD-app-M-why.text: Backs 3.5 (the systematised review: 43 networks, 16 countries, 47 ownership periods, 210 rows; owner coded twice; Fisher and permutation tests), 3.7 (limits) and 5.2 (46.0 per cent against 21.3 per cent, p = .008), with the same result repeated in 1.5, 5.4, 6.3, 6.5, 7.1 and 7.4.

AF-M-f1.speaker: marigold
AF-M-f1.text: 43 networks in 16 countries, 47 ownership periods, 210 rows of network-carrier evidence (207 distinct pairs).

AF-M-f2.speaker: marigold
AF-M-f2.text: Owner type was coded twice: class 42 of 47, alpha .87; neutral against rival-held 43 of 47, alpha .81.

AF-M-f3.speaker: marigold
AF-M-f3.text: Main test, each ownership period counted once: neutral-held networks reach 46.0% of a country's main carriers (12 periods), rival-held 21.3% (14 periods); permutation test p = .008.

AF-M-f4.speaker: marigold
AF-M-f4.text: Pairs with evidence: the carrier delivers in 45 of 48 neutral-held pairs (94%) and 18 of 44 rival-held (41%); Fisher p < .001.

AF-M-f5.speaker: marigold
AF-M-f5.text: Main carriers delivering: 41 of 88 (47%) against 18 of 86 (21%); Fisher p < .001.

AF-M-f6.speaker: marigold
AF-M-f6.text: The 26 ownership periods in the test cover 25 open networks.

AF-M-f7.speaker: marigold
AF-M-f7.text: Same carrier, different holders: by group 7 against 2 (10 equal), sign test p = .18; by national name 10 against 2 (9 equal), p = .039.

AF-M-f8.speaker: marigold
AF-M-f8.text: Two changes of holder are read both ways: the ex-A1 stations passing to Austrian Post (GLS stopped delivering) and De Buren passing to DHL Group in May 2025.

AF-M-f9.speaker: marigold
AF-M-f9.text: The myflexbox sale (announced 1 October 2026) gives a baseline: four weeks later the same five carriers are still listed as partners in Germany.

AF-M-f10.speaker: marigold
AF-M-f10.text: All searches were run and all pages accessed on 28 October 2026.

AF-M-f11.speaker: marigold
AF-M-f11.text: Only nine refusals by carriers are documented, two of them inferred; locker quality, price and terms were not measured.

AF-M-f12.speaker: marigold
AF-M-f12.text: Two rules were added once the networks had been listed, before the final run.

EQ-app-M-eq1.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-app-M-eq1.text: Doesn't this just show that neutral lockers are better lockers?

MA-app-M-eq1.speaker: marigold
MA-app-M-eq1.text: It might. The networks weren't matched on quality, price or terms, because no public measure of quality was found. The same-carrier check holds the carrier fixed but not the network. So it shows a difference by owner class, not cause, and I say so in M.1 and 3.7.

EQ-app-M-eq2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-app-M-eq2.text: Twenty-six ownership periods is a tiny sample.

MA-app-M-eq2.speaker: marigold
MA-app-M-eq2.text: It is, which is why I ran no regression and rest the result on a permutation test that counts each ownership period once: 46.0 per cent against 21.3, p = .008. The pair-level Fisher tests point the same way, but the pairs aren't independent, since one network serves several carriers, so those p-values are indicative only (5.2; M.1).

EQ-app-M-eq3.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-app-M-eq3.text: Does this test your claim that use falls as the holder's market commonality with each carrier rises?

MA-app-M-eq3.speaker: marigold
MA-app-M-eq3.text: No. Market commonality is coded by the holder's class, not measured pair by pair. The result is consistent with that gradient but doesn't test it, and I say so (M.1; 3.7).

EQ-app-M-eq4.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-app-M-eq4.text: What evidence is there that a sale changes who delivers?

MA-app-M-eq4.speaker: marigold

When the ex-A1 stations went to Austrian Post, GLS stopped delivering, but Austrian Post wouldn't say which cooperations continued, so there may be other causes. AF-D-f5.speaker: marigold

AF-D-f7.speaker: marigold

AF-D-f8.speaker: marigold

AF-D-f9.speaker: marigold

MA-app-D-eq1.speaker: marigold

I can't know whether anyone misread them, because the survey wasn't piloted. Every table that reports them states the direction, and I use the survey only for scale.

EQ-app-D-eq2.speaker: prof_kerbstone

MA-app-D-eq2.speaker: marigold

EQ-app-D-eq3.speaker: dr_tally

MA-app-D-eq3.speaker: marigold

That's why it tests no link: it describes, it doesn't explain (3.6).

EQ-app-D-eq4.speaker: prof_kerbstone

MA-app-D-eq4.speaker: marigold

AF-K-f7.speaker: marigold

EQ-app-K-eq1.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-app-K-eq1.text: With a self-selected sample and no response rate, what is this survey worth?

MA-app-K-eq1.speaker: marigold
MA-app-K-eq1.text: Scale, not inference. It's a non-probability sample that reached people along my networks; no response rate can be computed and none is claimed; no test of significance is run, and nothing is inferred to a population. I use it to set what organisations say about trust beside what the 117 arrangements show binds them (3.6; 5.3).

EQ-app-K-eq2.speaker: prof_kerbstone
EQ-app-K-eq2.text: 89 of 119 say trust is important. Doesn't that contradict your finding that trust doesn't bind?

MA-app-K-eq2.speaker: marigold
MA-app-K-eq2.text: No, it sits beside it. The survey records what people say matters; the arrangements show what actually held them. And among the 45 who said how they build trust, formal contracts, third-party coordination and public authority support were named beside joint planning. Saying trust matters and relying on outside binders aren't in conflict (5.3).

EQ-app-K-eq3.speaker: dr_tally
EQ-app-K-eq3.text: Why do companies that don't collaborate answer questions meant for those that do?

MA-app-K-eq3.speaker: marigold

I read those as past or expected collaboration, and I say the challenges item can't tell a challenge met in an earlier attempt from one that's expected (3.6).

EQ-app-K-eq4.speaker: prof_kerbstone

MA-app-K-eq4.speaker: marigold

EQ-app-K-eq5.speaker: dr_tally

MA-app-K-eq5.speaker: marigold
MA-app-K-eq5.text: It's high partly because the codebook was drawn up from these same 39 answers in the first coding, which makes agreement easier in so short a set. The second coding was blind, from the codebook and the answers alone, and I report the agreement with that limit (3.6).

VR-thesis.one_sentence.speaker: marigold
VR-thesis.one_sentence.text: Competition for the same customers, not a shortage of trust, is what stops last-mile carriers collaborating; where they cannot share the street, what they would share must be held by someone who does not want their customers, and a city can see that it stays that way.

VR-thesis.aim.speaker: marigold
VR-thesis.aim.text: This research focuses on the conditions under which horizontal collaboration succeeds in European urban last-mile logistics, why it so rarely does between competing carriers, and whether its aims can be achieved by other means.

VR-thesis.research_question.speaker: marigold
VR-thesis.research_question.text: Under what conditions does horizontal collaboration in European urban last-mile logistics succeed, and what achieves its aims where it does not?

VR-link-1.speaker: marigold
VR-link-1.text: Where rivals' markets overlap, they refuse to pool what could expose their customers, unless a wall, a penalty or an owner with no stake in those customers outweighs that exposure; the carrier's size does not predict the refusal.

VR-link-2.speaker: marigold
VR-link-2.text: Where collaboration between carriers does happen, what is shared is space, facilities, vehicles and infrastructure, what is withheld is customers and operating data, and the freight crosses the line only where a third party, a reciprocal contract or a reputation system secures what would otherwise be exposed, which is why the shared van of 1.2 so rarely arrived; where freight is pooled, as in the shipper-led schemes Chapter 2 reads, it is the owners of the freight who pooled it.

VR-link-3.speaker: marigold
VR-link-3.text: What holds most of those arrangements together is not trust between the parties but something that binds them from outside: a neutral third party, a grant, a regulation, permit or mandate, a contract, a client's instruction, a prior vertical relationship, a reciprocal trade or a platform's reputation.

VR-link-4.speaker: marigold
VR-link-4.text: The parties who can supply that binding sit mainly on the demand side and the public side: shippers, receivers and cities.

VR-link-5.speaker: marigold
VR-link-5.text: And so, the thesis proposes, the aims that collaboration is asked to deliver can be reached another way: the shared point passes to a holder that does not compete for the carriers' customers, an access rule by vehicle and hour that names no operator makes it worth doing, and the city checks, every time the holder changes hands, that it still does not compete, buying that neutrality on its own land and requiring conduct at the points it permits.

VR-P1.speaker: marigold
VR-P1.text: Unless a wall, a penalty or an owner with no stake outweighs the exposure, the willingness of two last-mile operators to collaborate falls as the overlap of their customer markets rises.

VR-P2.speaker: marigold
VR-P2.text: The more a shared resource constitutes a party's customer relationship, the less likely it is to be pooled.

VR-P3.speaker: marigold
VR-P3.text: A horizontal collaboration lasts as long as the external arrangement that binds it.

VR-P4.speaker: marigold
VR-P4.text: An instrument aimed at the party that places the order or writes the permit changes last-mile flows more than the same instrument aimed at the party that carries the goods.

VR-P5.speaker: marigold
VR-P5.text: At equal access, a carrier's use of a shared point falls as the holder's market commonality with that carrier rises.

OBJ-1.speaker: marigold
OBJ-1.text: The research will identify the conditions under which last-mile operators agree to collaborate horizontally, and those under which they decline.

OBJ-1A.speaker: marigold
OBJ-1A.text: It will assess how willingness varies with the size of the operator.

OBJ-1B.speaker: marigold
OBJ-1B.text: It will assess how willingness varies with the extent to which the parties' markets overlap.

OBJ-1C.speaker: marigold
OBJ-1C.text: It will compare these across the eleven countries studied, ten of them European.

OBJ-2.speaker: marigold
OBJ-2.text: It will examine what is shared in the collaborations that operate, what is withheld, and the line between them.

OBJ-2A.speaker: marigold
OBJ-2A.text: It will identify what is pooled.

OBJ-2B.speaker: marigold
OBJ-2B.text: It will identify what is withheld.

OBJ-2C.speaker: marigold
OBJ-2C.text: It will explain, from participants' accounts, where the line falls and why.

OBJ-3.speaker: marigold
OBJ-3.text: It will explain what holds working collaborations together.

OBJ-3A.speaker: marigold
OBJ-3A.text: It will assess the part played by trust between the parties.

OBJ-3B.speaker: marigold
OBJ-3B.text: It will identify the arrangements supplied from outside the parties.

OBJ-3C.speaker: marigold
OBJ-3C.text: It will evaluate how long each has lasted.

OBJ-4.speaker: marigold
OBJ-4.text: It will establish where in the supply chain the power to reorganise last-mile flows sits.

OBJ-4A.speaker: marigold
OBJ-4A.text: It will assess that power among carriers.

OBJ-4B.speaker: marigold
OBJ-4B.text: It will assess it among shippers and receivers.

OBJ-4C.speaker: marigold
OBJ-4C.text: It will assess it among public authorities.

OBJ-5.speaker: marigold
OBJ-5.text: It will evaluate what achieves the aims attributed to collaboration where collaboration between competing carriers does not.

OBJ-5A.speaker: marigold
OBJ-5A.text: It will identify the aims attributed to collaboration, as stated by the field and by participants.

OBJ-5B.speaker: marigold
OBJ-5B.text: It will evaluate whether partitioning the last mile in time, rather than pooling it, achieves them, in the operating instance of time-based allocation in the record.

OBJ-5C.speaker: marigold
OBJ-5C.text: It will evaluate whether the holder of the shared point where rivals meet affects whether carriers share it, and assess the objections and the limits.

PROP-P1-fals.speaker: marigold
PROP-P1-fals.text: a sample of operators with no wall, penalty or neutral holder between them in which willingness does not fall with overlap at some size band, or in which size sorts willingness where overlap does not

PROP-P2-fals.speaker: marigold
PROP-P2-fals.text: a working arrangement between rivals in the urban last mile that pools freight, customers or operating data with nothing binding it

PROP-P3-fals.speaker: marigold
PROP-P3-fals.text: an arrangement that outlived its binder on the parties' trust alone, or that dissolved while its binder stood and its parties still gained

PROP-P4-fals.speaker: marigold
PROP-P4-fals.text: an instrument aimed at carriers, a price or a rule, that moved flows more than the same instrument aimed at receivers or cities

PROP-P5-fals.speaker: marigold
PROP-P5-fals.text: no difference in carriers' use by holder at equal access, or no change in carriers' partner lists after a sale to a rival

BQ-pro-26.text: P2 says the more a resource constitutes a party's customer relationship, the less likely it is to be pooled. What would falsify it?

BF-pro-26.speaker: prof_kerbstone
BF-pro-26.text: The rural case shares runs with nothing binding it. Why doesn't that falsify P2?

BQ-pro-27.speaker: dr_tally
BQ-pro-27.text: Three of your cases pass freight between rivals: the cross-border swap, the courier platform and the trustee's pooled distribution. Why doesn't any of them falsify P2?

BF-pro-27.speaker: dr_tally
BF-pro-27.text: Take away the platform's reviews and insurance. Would the courier exchange then falsify P2?

BQ-pro-28.speaker: prof_kerbstone
BQ-pro-28.text: A southern capital's shippers' hub pools freight and the participant named no binder. Isn't that P2's falsifier sitting in your own record?

BF-pro-28.speaker: prof_kerbstone
BF-pro-28.text: What would you need to learn about that hub to settle the row?

BQ-pro-29.speaker: dr_tally
BQ-pro-29.text: P3 says a collaboration lasts as long as the external arrangement that binds it. What would falsify it?

BF-pro-29.speaker: dr_tally
BF-pro-29.text: Why doesn't the cargo-bike operator's move to a new hub count as dissolving while its binder stood?

BQ-pro-30.speaker: prof_kerbstone
BQ-pro-30.text: Four of your rows ran on peer trust alone, with no binder at all. Why aren't they the 'outlived its binder on trust alone' case that falsifies P3?

BF-pro-30.speaker: prof_kerbstone
BF-pro-30.text: If the two couriers bid jointly again next year with nothing binding them, what would that do to P3?

BQ-pro-31.speaker: dr_tally
BQ-pro-31.text: P3 came from the 117 rows. How would someone test it on data that didn't produce it?

BF-pro-31.speaker: dr_tally
BF-pro-31.text: Which class of binder would you sample first, and why?

BQ-pro-32.speaker: prof_kerbstone
BQ-pro-32.text: P4 says an instrument aimed at whoever places the order or writes the permit moves flows more than one aimed at the carrier. What would falsify it?

BF-pro-32.speaker: prof_kerbstone
BF-pro-32.text: Is there any instrument in your record aimed at carriers that did move flows?

BQ-pro-33.speaker: dr_tally
BQ-pro-33.text: Your evidence for P4 is accounts and who began each row. Couldn't a carrier-aimed instrument still beat a receiver-aimed one, and you'd never know?

BF-pro-33.speaker: dr_tally
BF-pro-33.text: What would that comparison look like in a city that prices both carriers and receivers?

BQ-pro-34.speaker: prof_kerbstone
BQ-pro-34.text: Holguín-Veras's toll fell on carriers, and only 9 per cent could pass it on. Isn't one New York study the whole of P4?

BF-pro-34.speaker: prof_kerbstone
BF-pro-34.text: What would a receiver-aimed version of the same toll look like?
